e: Obregón, President of Mexico, chose the licenciado José Vasconcelos as Secretary of Federal Public Education, unanimous opinion had already made that choice. It has been one of those cases, infrequent everywhere, in which the judgement of the ruler and that of the ruled are one and the same; the explanation is simple: Vasconcelos has a high significance within the Mexican revolution, and outside it he has one too. His worth is not circumstantial but specific, and therefore permanent. His ideas, everyone knows, are radical; but even within his revolutionary radicalism he is an eminently constructive spirit. For him the revolution must be as creative as possible and as little destructive as possible. He knows that one of our basic problems is the de-donkeying of our humblest social strata; that every social edifice built upon an uneducated and unconscious mass is tinsel and crumbling; and for that reason we see him struggle, with a devotion not merely of a good ruler but of a good apostle, in the branch of Public Instruction. He has set out his judgement on other occasions: he does not wish to follow a rigid preconceived plan, but to resolve each case according to the needs of the moment; not adapting reality, always diverse, to a rigid theory, always the same, but adapting theories to realities. This man of the library has not let himself be seduced by bookish orientations; he goes with the dynamism of life, converting into action what he draws from books. With Vasconcelos there is no fear that he will sweat printer’s ink, as someone once said, alluding to the excess

o: de lecturas del hombre moderno, el cual exceso hizo exclamar a Amiel ansioso de un purgante para el inlecto: se lee demasiado. Si el genio tiene tan alta significación es por su capacidad para servir más que a los otros a las multitudes, ha escrito Vasconcelos. Vamos viendo que el flamante Secretario de Instrucción no ha hecho suyo el evangelio del arte por el arte. Un hondo sentido cristalino de la vida, de la solidaridad humana, de la propia responsabilidad ante el problema de la evolución social, lo posee. Por eso fué revolucionario en el momento histórico que le, tocó vivir, por eso quiere construir lo más y destruir lo menos y por eso le viene, a la medida, la Secretaría de Educación. A través de su radicalismo, de sus apasionamientos, al tratar a Vasconcelos se le encuentra pronto “la tibia leche de la bondad humana.” Rodó, el gran estilista, quería que se perdiera mucho tiempo en primores de estilo: es, decía como si el tiempo de labrar se invirtiera en cinceladuras para los utensilios de labranza y Vasconcelos, con su manera combativa asienta: “quisiéramos que EL MAESTRO iniciara a nuestros escritores en un nuevo período, que bien podríamos llamar antiliterario y que sirviera para decir las cosas como son, muy lejos de la tiranía de la forma, muy lejos del vano fantasma de la gloria.” Algunos atribuyen falta de sentido práctico a Vasconcelos. Los que así piensan, juzgan que ser práctico es ser oportunista. Si así fuera Vasconcelos, sería el hombre menos práctico. Pero él tiene un sentido exacto de las realidades; sólo que no quiere someterse a ellas sino cuando concuerdan con su concepto de la justicia y del bien. Daremos algunos datos biográficos de este hombre, fuerza mental de nuestro país y orgullo de nuestra revolución. Nació José Vasconcelos en la ciudad de Oaxaca, el año de 1882. Su famila se distinguió siempre por el amor a las letras y un honesto vivir: es la suya de las antiguas familias oaxaqueñas. Su padre fué aquel probo e integro don Ignacio Vasconcelos. Allá, en su pueblo natal, recibió la primera deficiente instrucción
e: of reading of modern man, an excess which made Amiel, anxious for a purgative for the intellect, exclaim: one reads too much. If genius has so high a significance, it is because of its capacity to serve the multitudes more than others do, Vasconcelos has written. We see that the brand-new Secretary of Instruction has not made the gospel of art for art’s sake his own. He possesses a deep crystalline sense of life, of human solidarity, of his own responsibility before the problem of social evolution. For that reason he was a revolutionary in the historical moment it fell to him to live through, for that reason he wishes to build the most and destroy the least, and for that reason the Secretariat of Education suits him to the measure. Through his radicalism, through his passions, on dealing with Vasconcelos one soon finds in him “the tepid milk of human kindness.” Rodó, the great stylist, wanted much time to be spent on refinements of style: it is, he said, as if the time for tilling were spent in chiselling ornaments on the tools of tillage; and Vasconcelos, in his combative manner, asserts: “we should like THE TEACHER to initiate our writers into a new period, which we might well call antiliterary, and which would serve to say things as they are, far from the tyranny of form, far from the vain phantom of glory.” Some attribute a lack of practical sense to Vasconcelos. Those who think so judge that to be practical is to be an opportunist. If that were so, Vasconcelos would be the least practical of men. But he has an exact sense of realities; only he will not submit to them except when they accord with his conception of justice and of the good. We shall give some biographical data about this man, a mental force of our country and the pride of our revolution. José Vasconcelos was born in the city of Oaxaca in the year 1882. His family was always distinguished by a love of letters and an honest way of life: it is one of the old Oaxacan families. His father was that upright and honourable don Ignacio Vasconcelos. There, in his native town, he received the first, deficient instruction

o: que se daba en la época. Se trasladó a la ciudad de México, andando el el tiempo, para cursar estudios superiores. Fué un aprovechado preparatoriano. Cuando terminó estos estudios, ingresó en la Escuela de Jurisprudencia, que estaba entonces en eledificio que hoy se reconstruye para la Secretaría de Educación. Allí trabó, con sus compañeros, amistades que hoy conserva: a Isidro Fabela, a Miguel Alessio Robles, fraternales amigos suyos, allí los conoció. Desde aquella lejana época se le despertó el interés que hoy tiene por los asuntos del Oriente ignoto y legendario. En 1905 terminó su carrera de abogado. Presentó para obtener su título una bella tesis: TEORIA DINAMICA DEL DERECHO, la cual fué justificadamente aplaudida por el Jurado Calificador. Ya de abogado fué electo Agente del Ministerio Público adscrito al Estado de Durango. En este cargo permaneció muy poco tiempo, Desde el año de 1908, comenzó Vasconcelos en su apostolado revolucionario. En 1909 se fundó el partido Antirreeleccionista. Vasconcelos que era uno de sus miembros más prominentes, fué nombrado director del órgano de publicidad de aquel partido: un semanario llamado “El Antirreeleccionista.” Llenando brillantemente su función estuvo hasta que dejó el honroso cargo a otro activo revolucionario, el ingeniero Félix F. Palavicini actual gerente de “El Universal”. Ya para entonces el semanario se había convertido en diario. La labor de “El Antirreeleccionista” es suficientemente conocida de nuestro público. Sus columnas fueron la primera tribuna del verbo revolucionario. En ese mismo año se constituyó el Ateneo de México, integrado por pretigiados intelectuales y jóvenes llenos de férvida dedicación a las letras. Los ateneístas supieron lo que hicieron al elegir al jóven escritor como presidente de la novísima sociedad. Al llegar el apóstol y mártir Madero en su activa campaña democrática a esta ciudad de México, formó el Partido Constitucional Progre
e: that was given at the time. In the course of time he moved to Mexico City to pursue higher studies. He was a diligent preparatory student. When he finished these studies he entered the School of Jurisprudence, which was then in the building now being rebuilt for the Secretariat of Education. There he formed, with his companions, friendships which he keeps today: Isidro Fabela and Miguel Alessio Robles, brotherly friends of his, he met there. From that distant time there awoke in him the interest which he has today in the affairs of the unknown and legendary Orient. In 1905 he completed his career as a lawyer. To obtain his title he presented a beautiful thesis: TEORIA DINAMICA DEL DERECHO, which was deservedly applauded by the examining Jury. Already a lawyer, he was elected Agent of the Public Ministry attached to the State of Durango. He remained in this post a very short time. From the year 1908 Vasconcelos began his revolutionary apostolate. In 1909 the Anti-Reelectionist party was founded. Vasconcelos, who was one of its most prominent members, was appointed director of the organ of publicity of that party: a weekly called “El Antirreeleccionista.” He brilliantly filled his function until he left the honourable post to another active revolutionary, the engineer Félix F. Palavicini, now manager of “El Universal.” By then the weekly had become a daily. The work of “El Antirreeleccionista” is sufficiently well known to our public. Its columns were the first tribune of the revolutionary word. In that same year the Ateneo de México was constituted, made up of prestigious intellectuals and young men full of fervent dedication to letters. The members of the Ateneo knew what they were doing when they elected the young writer president of the brand-new society. When the apostle and martyr Madero, in his active democratic campaign, reached this city of Mexico, he formed the Progressive Constitutional

o: sista. Miembro del Comité Ejecutivo de dicho Partido fué el licenciado Vasconcelos. La revolución se vió precisada, para impouer, a ir a la guerra en 1910. Don Francisco I. Madero lo nombró su representante en Washington, para que la mencionada cancillería reconocíera la beligerencia de los revolucionarios. En esta misión obtuvo brillante éxito Vasconcelos. Gracias a su habilidad diplomática, del Norte llegaron a los campos revolucionarios tode clase de elementos de guerra. Triunfante la revolución, se le ofrecieron al férvido revolucionario cargos oficiales que no aceptó, para ir a California a resolver asuntos de su profesión. Permaneció allí hasta que tuvo efecto el asesinato de Madero. Al saber que un varón fuerte y patriota, don Venustiano Carranza, levantaba el estandarte de la revolución en trance de muerte, fué a su lado a cumplir su deder de ciudadano. Carranza lo nombró mny acertadamente Enviado Especial de la revolución constitucionalista ante los Gobiernos de Francia, Inglaterra y España. Vasconcelos retornó de su misión cuando entraron triunfantes a la capital las fuerzas constitucionalistas. Entonces fué nombrado Director de la Preparatoria. Tocó a su antiguo compañero de causa, el ingeniero Pala vicini, presidir la toma de posesión como Secretario del Ramo. Vasconce los recuerda con afecto el encomiástico discurso del ingeniero Palavicini. Poco después se distanció de Carranza y se expatrió voluntariamente. Al mes regresaba al país y formaba filas con los convencionistas. Fué como delegado de este grupo a la Soberana Convención de Aguascalientes. El Presidente Provisional de la República, general Eulalio Gutiérrez eligió a Vasconcelos para Secretario de Instrucción Pública. En talcargo fué amenazado de muerte por Zapata. Vasconcelos, lleno energía, no huyó como se le aconsejaba; muy al contrario, permaneció eu su cargo hasta redactar aquel conocido Manifiesto a la Nación que firmó Gutiérrez antes de abandonar la metrópoli. e: Party. The licenciado Vasconcelos was a member of the Executive Committee of that Party. The revolution found itself compelled, in order to prevail, to go to war in 1910. Don Francisco I. Madero named him his representative in Washington, so that the aforesaid chancellery might recognise the belligerency of the revolutionaries. In this mission Vasconcelos obtained brilliant success. Thanks to his diplomatic skill, every kind of war matériel reached the revolutionary camps from the North. With the revolution triumphant, official posts were offered to the fervent revolutionary, which he did not accept, in order to go to California to settle matters of his profession. He remained there until the assassination of Madero took place. On learning that a strong and patriotic man, don Venustiano Carranza, was raising the standard of the revolution in its death throes, he went to his side to fulfil his duty as a citizen. Carranza very fittingly named him Special Envoy of the constitutionalist revolution to the Governments of France, England and Spain. Vasconcelos returned from his mission when the constitutionalist forces entered the capital in triumph. He was then appointed Director of the Preparatoria. It fell to his old comrade in the cause, the engineer Palavicini, to preside, as Secretary of the Department, over his taking of office. Vasconcelos remembers with affection the laudatory speech of the engineer Palavicini. A little later he became estranged from Carranza and voluntarily expatriated himself. A month later he returned to the country and joined the ranks of the Conventionists. He went as delegate of this group to the Sovereign Convention of Aguascalientes. The Provisional President of the Republic, General Eulalio Gutiérrez, chose Vasconcelos as Secretary of Public Instruction. In that post he was threatened with death by Zapata. Vasconcelos, full of energy, did not flee as he was advised to; quite the contrary, he remained at his post until he had drafted that well-known Manifesto to the Nation which Gutiérrez signed before abandoning the metropolis. He emigrated again

o: y se estableció por algún tiempo en Nueva York, en donde ejerció de abogado. Más tarde en uno de de sus libros, ha recordado Vasconcelos con la melancolía del buen tiempo pasado su vida limeña. Es oportuno hacer constar una interesante faz de Vasconcelos: su hispanoamericanismo. Siente como el que más la solidaridad de estos pueblos, unos en sus cualidades y defectos y que atraviesan ciclos sociológicos con diferencias mínimas. José Martí, refiriéndose a las Antillas, escribió que se salvarían o se perderían juntas, y Vasconcelos sabe que la frase de Martí queda siendo cierto aún, extendiéndola a todo nuestro Continente de origen hispánico. Cuando defendemos la integridad y dignidad de no importa cuál de nuestro países, estamos defendiendo, la integridad y la dignidad de toda nuestra América Española. Si sus libros no fueran suficien. te para hablarnos del hispanoamericanismo de Vasconcelos, ahí esta su simpática actitud de revolucionario venezolano, que lo llevó hasta jugar su posición oficial al combatir abiertamente la tiranía instintiva de Juan Vicente Gómez. El año pasado fué elegido por el Presidente Provisional, señor Adolfo de la Huerta, Rector de la Universidad, cargo en donde con nna con. sagración como ya dijimos, de apóstol, ha laborado con sabiduría y entusiasmo, educaudo e instruyendo a las masas: Al palpar el inconveniente de que no estuviera federalizada la instrucción, se dió a la tarea de federalizarla y fué de pueblo en pueblo persuadiendo a los interesados, por medio de conferencias, en una democrática jira, de la urgencia nacional de la creación de la flamante Secretaría,
e: and settled for some time in New York, where he practised as a lawyer. In 1916 he obtained, for South America, the representation of an American Correspondence School Company. On this account he moved to Lima, where he lived for long months and where he left the most pleasant memory. There he made cordial friendships with the representatives of Peruvian intellectual life; there he met Riva-Agüero, the critic, and Valdelomar, the poet; there, finally, before a crowded public he delivered a lecture which in our opinion is the most beautifully written and the most deeply thought thing that has come from his pen. Later, in one of his books, Vasconcelos has recalled his Lima life with the melancholy of the good time past. It is fitting to put on record an interesting aspect of Vasconcelos: his Hispano-Americanism. He feels, as much as anyone, the solidarity of these peoples, one in their qualities and defects and passing through sociological cycles with minimal differences. José Martí, referring to the Antilles, wrote that they would be saved or lost together, and Vasconcelos knows that Martí’s phrase remains true still, if extended to our whole Continent of Hispanic origin. When we defend the integrity and dignity of no matter which of our countries, we are defending the integrity and the dignity of all our Spanish America. If his books were not enough to tell us of Vasconcelos’s Hispano-Americanism, there is his sympathetic attitude as a Venezuelan revolutionary, which led him even to stake his official position by openly combating the instinctive tyranny of Juan Vicente Gómez. Last year he was chosen by the Provisional President, señor Adolfo de la Huerta, as Rector of the University, a post in which, with a devotion, as we have said, of an apostle, he has laboured with wisdom and enthusiasm, educating and instructing the masses. On perceiving the drawback that instruction was not federalised, he set himself to the task of federalising it, and went from town to town, persuading those concerned, by means of lectures, on a democratic tour, of the national urgency of creating the brand-new Secretariat.

e: To the students of Trujillo who addressed me in the name of the students of Peru.] SINCE I received the message in which you informed me that you had named me your teacher, I resolved to write to you at length, but not only have my preoccupations, at times disconsolate, and my occupations, always absorbing, held me back, but also the fear of complicating with my words a situation already dangerous in itself; a fear all the more justified in that I cannot come to share your hardships, and it is therefore very compromising to send you counsels with impunity and from a distance. Indeed, what can I say to you in the face of the situation you are in, in the face of the state in which this whole contemporary world finds itself, plagued with injustice and hatred; in the face of all this triumph of Cain there in Peru and here in Mexico and in almost every place where men live today! Lacerated by another’s hatred when they have felt love overflowing, that is, I imagine, the situation of all the noble souls of the world. One does not wish to believe in evil; it seems to us an absurdity and an error of

También debo reflexionar en que hablo a jóvenes de ánimo ardiente y no puedo permitir que un descorazonamiento mío, aunque sea pasajero, los contagie. Si he de mencionarles penas, lo haré para mostrarme enteramente sincero y para que se den cuenta de la enormidad de la tarea que tiene delante de sí todo el que combate por un ideal; no para desanimarlos, sino para que se apeguen con más afán a la empresa reformadora, a la tarea sin fin que no se consuma con una sola victoria, ni con derrocar un tirano es preciso derrocar a cada tirano - sino que debe renovarse una y otra vez; siu descanso y sin ilusión, pegando sin tregua contra los grandes obstáculos y también contra los ruines contratiempos que agotan oscuramente el anhelo. Duro es el camino del ideal sin reservas, quien lo siga ha de contar de antemano con la desilusión y el infortunio y deberá examinar su conciencia para ver si posee algo de la sustancia de lo que se yergue. El que ambicione dicha o se complazca con la comodidad y la fama que nadie disputa, póngase en la frente la coyunda de las ideas corrientes y con buena salud y un poco de esfuerzo alcanzará ventura y hará los suyos felices, siempre que cuide de dar su parte al más fuerte, y la razón, no tanto a quien la tiene, sino más bien a quien la impone. Hombres así suelen ser útiles y sin duda merecen su dicha tranquila y ruin. Ustedes que son jóvenes deberán interrogarse sinceramente, y si es la felicidad lo que ambicionan, no vacilen, háganse cuerdos, desarrollen ingenio y fuerza y todos los tesoros del mundo llegarán a ser suyos. Pero si en el fondo del corazón han sentido
e: easy correction, but it bites and rends, so that if we examine ourselves within, we feel undone; but this, in the end, comes of much struggling, and passes quickly, and in reality life is worth only for its noble instants, which one must strive to live though all the rest be lost. I must also reflect that I am speaking to young men of ardent spirit and cannot allow a disheartenment of mine, though it be passing, to infect them. If I am to mention sorrows, I shall do so in order to show myself entirely sincere and so that you may realise the enormity of the task that lies before everyone who fights for an ideal; not to dishearten you, but so that you may cleave with more eagerness to the reforming enterprise, to the endless task which is not consummated with a single victory, nor with the overthrow of a tyrant — one must overthrow each tyrant — but must be renewed again and again; without rest and without illusion, striking without truce against the great obstacles and also against the petty setbacks that obscurely exhaust longing. Hard is the road of the ideal without reservations; whoever follows it must count beforehand on disillusion and misfortune and must examine his conscience to see whether he possesses something of the substance of what rises up. Let him who covets happiness or is pleased with comfort and uncontested fame put on his brow the yoke of current ideas, and with good health and a little effort he will attain good fortune and make his own people happy, provided he takes care to give his share to the strongest, and the right, not so much to him who has it, as rather to him who imposes it. Men of this kind are often useful and doubtless deserve their tranquil and mean happiness. You who are young must question yourselves sincerely, and if it is happiness that you covet, do not hesitate, make yourselves sensible, develop ingenuity and strength and all the treasures of the world will become yours. But if in the depth of your heart you have felt

o: una sorda inquietud, que no se satisface nicon el lucro, ni con la falsa fama, ni con la dicha ruin, entonces todavía deténganse a pensarlo, porque el camino es árduo. Si a pesar de todo eso se sienten movidos por un afán que se atreve a todo, y padecen el disgusto de la verdad incompleta; de la dicha infecunda; si el día que termina sin un suceso ilustre les causa angustia; si el ansia de la vida infinita los llena de un dolor confuso que nada cura del todo; si una sed de ser y de gloria les devora las entrañas; si están dispuestos a padecer; resueltos a no hacer otra cosa que sufrir por toda una vida de martirio y grandeza, entonces, serán de los elegidos. Pero estén seguros de que les esperan la indiferencia y la po. breza, el escándalo, la persecución y el odio; seguros de que causarán la desdicha de los que aman; de que sufrirán separaciones lacerantes, y en seguida la calumnia y la burla, el desdén y la saña, el presidio, el destierro y quizás la muerte. Y aún antes que la muerte física, la muerte del sentimiento en un desgarrarse de todos los afectos y un perder cuanto se ama. Vendrán después las horas rápidas, momentáneas del triunfo y padecerán entonces de un mirar claro que revela la miseria de gentes y cosas; de un no poder creer, de un ya no querer nada que se refugia en los días mismos del infortunio, porque en ellos había siquiera la profundidad infinita del dolor sin consuelo; seguirán mirando como unos sonámbulos, las cosas de la tierra, y con el alma perdida en un vago infinito que a veces guía, pero que frecuentemente nos deja solos. Y así que hayan concluído la tarea, o cuando apenas esté iniciada, quizás verán que se reanudan las persecuciones, las penas, las inquietudes sin término, hasta que la muerte se les aparezca como una positiva liberación. Si desean arrostrar todo ésto, a cambio de unos breves instantes de verdad resplandeciente o de pasión sin freno, se sentirán invencibles, y por mucho que los atormenten podrán
e: a dull restlessness, which is satisfied neither by gain, nor by false fame, nor by mean happiness, then still pause to think it over, because the road is arduous. If in spite of all that you feel moved by a longing that dares everything, and suffer the distaste of incomplete truth, of barren happiness; if the day that ends without an illustrious event causes you anguish; if the craving for infinite life fills you with a confused pain that nothing wholly cures; if a thirst for being and for glory devours your entrails; if you are ready to suffer; resolved to do nothing else but suffer through a whole life of martyrdom and greatness, then you will be among the chosen. But be sure that indifference and poverty await you, scandal, persecution and hatred; sure that you will cause the unhappiness of those you love; that you will suffer lacerating separations, and soon after calumny and mockery, disdain and fury, imprisonment, exile and perhaps death. And even before physical death, the death of feeling in a tearing apart of all the affections and a losing of whatever one loves. Then will come the swift, momentary hours of triumph, and you will suffer from a clear gaze that reveals the misery of people and things; from a not being able to believe, from a no longer wanting anything that takes refuge in the very days of misfortune, because in them there was at least the infinite depth of grief without consolation; you will go on looking, like sleepwalkers, at the things of the earth, and with the soul lost in a vague infinite that sometimes guides, but frequently leaves us alone. And as soon as you have concluded the task, or when it is barely begun, perhaps you will see that the persecutions, the sorrows, the endless disquiets begin again, until death appears to you as a positive liberation. If you wish to face all this, in exchange for a few brief instants of resplendent truth or of unbridled passion, you will feel invincible, and however much they torment you, you will be able

o: seguir adelante, sin que nada pueda tocarlos; ni el dolor, que si es grande y encuentra en ustedes temple, roza como el arco en la cuerda, para crear sonoridad y alegría, ni la muerte que si es heroica, enciende un más vivo anhelo! Podrán seguir adelante contra los despotismos de la tierra y contra los abusos de la mente, desarrollando todas las capacidades para que trabajen por el triunfo de la acción libre y de la locura generosa. No estén entonces cuerdos, ni un sólo instante; batallen y forjen sin descanso; en patrias como éstas, no hacer es un pecado y todo lo demás es virtud. Obren en grande pensando en belleza. Suelten sus fuerzas como río desbordado pero consciente de que remueve la tierra y fecunda inmensidades. Nadie podra detener el impulso de una juventud unida y activa, generosa y libre. Usen su fuerza para derribar la tiranía del hombre, la tiranía de las instituciones y la tiranía de los propios apetitos. Y para todo ésto, venzan primero en ustedes mismos; renuncien la vida dulce, para merecer la vida sublime. Los jóvenes que aspiran a dirigir pueblos y a redimir gentes, podrán conocer la pasión, pero no tienen tiempo para los deleites. Quienes prefieren la voluptuosidad al deslumbramiento, no serán intérpretes del afán colectivo; ni gozarán jamás el transporte de sentirse como instrumento divino de los procesos humanos. La valiente actitud que ustedes han comenzado a desarrollar me obliga a enviarles la palabra de mi experiencia; también el afecto me inclina a sufrir con las penalidades que azotan al Perú. No debemos ser indiferentes al dolor de nin. gún pueblo de la tierra, mucho menos al de un pueblo que es porción de nuestra patria ibero americana. No puedo olvidar tampoco lo que debo personalmente al Perú en los
e: to go forward, with nothing able to touch you; neither grief, which, if it is great and finds temper in you, grazes you as the bow does the string, to create sonority and joy, nor death, which, if it is heroic, kindles a livelier longing! You will be able to go forward against the despotisms of the earth and against the abuses of the mind, developing all your capacities to work for the triumph of free action and of generous madness. Do not be sensible, then, not for a single instant; battle and forge without rest; in fatherlands like these, not to act is a sin and everything else is virtue. Act greatly, thinking of beauty. Loose your forces like a river in flood, but conscious that it turns up the earth and fertilises immensities. No one will be able to halt the impulse of a youth united and active, generous and free. Use your strength to overthrow the tyranny of man, the tyranny of institutions and the tyranny of your own appetites. And for all this, conquer first in yourselves; renounce the sweet life, to deserve the sublime life. Young men who aspire to lead peoples and to redeem men can know passion, but have no time for delights. Those who prefer voluptuousness to dazzlement will not be interpreters of the collective longing; nor will they ever enjoy the transport of feeling themselves an instrument divine of the human processes. The valiant attitude you have begun to develop obliges me to send you the word of my experience; affection too inclines me to suffer with the hardships that scourge Peru. We must not be indifferent to the pain of any people on earth, much less to that of a people that is a portion of our Ibero-American fatherland. Nor can I forget what I personally owe to Peru in the

o: días en que era libre y yo arribé allá perseguido y sin más título que el de ser un mexicano que había sido perseguido por todos los dictadores de su patria, y eso me abrió todas las puertas y me ganó todos los pechos. Como la visión de una vida aparte, guardo el recuerdo de aquel viaje, y tiem. blo de pensar en la emoción de un retorno a Lima, me coge. ría el ambiente, y tendría que volver a vivir las horas profundas, las horas amargas, los ásperos deleites, la asombrosa; la desgarradora vida de mis diez meses de amor, de desesperación y de videncia. Fué aquello un conflicto de placi. dez de afuera y la tempestad que llevaba adentro, y tanto anegué mi alma en cosas y gentes, que todavía me parece que sigo envuelto como en un aura que volvería a poseerme entera si concentrase mis recuerdos un instante. Sin embarga, los años no pasan en balde; el tiempo nos purifica, dicen los necios; yo más bien creo que nos roba, nos desvanece el tesoro, de las emociones, nos deja viles y pobres; viles porque olvidamos, pobres, porque perdemos porciones de la misma existencia, así es como aquel vivir profundo se me ha ido haciendo sueño. Y ya ahora sólo guardo la visión refulgente de las moles andinas, que trepé todo un día asombroso y la noche estrellada de la Oroya y los ríos y las planicies y las cumbres de nieve y las grandes olas encrespadas de sonidos y de espuma, y el mar vigorizante verde, impregnado de su potencia, que penetró en todos mis poros. Veo las tabernas oscuras del Callao, en donde vagabundos de todo el planeta, bebíamos aguardiente de Pisco igual que si fuera un cauterio de heridas sangrantes. Pasan más gentes, las jóvenes lindas, las matronas de ojos que humedece la ternura, los amigos cordiales y me asalta la amargura de una vida que no volverá. Veo los desfiles militares acompañados de músicas tristes, monótonas, que me hinchan, el pecho de patriotismo peruano, un patriotismo que yo interpretaba co mo la afirmación
e: days when it was free and I arrived there persecuted and with no other title than that of being a Mexican who had been persecuted by all the dictators of his fatherland, and that opened every door to me and won me every heart. Like the vision of a life apart, I keep the memory of that journey, and I tremble to think of the emotion of a return to Lima; the atmosphere would seize me, and I should have to live again the profound hours, the bitter hours, the harsh delights, the astonishing, the heart-rending life of my ten months of love, of despair and of vision. It was a conflict between the placidity outside and the tempest I carried within, and so deeply did I drown my soul in things and people that I still seem to go on wrapped as in an aura that would possess me whole again if I were to concentrate my memories for an instant. And yet the years do not pass in vain; time purifies us, say fools; I rather believe that it robs us, dissolves for us the treasure of the emotions, leaves us base and poor; base because we forget, poor because we lose portions of existence itself; thus it is that that profound living has been turning into a dream for me. And now I keep only the refulgent vision of the Andean masses, which I climbed through a whole astonishing day, and the starry night of La Oroya and the rivers and the plains and the snowy summits and the great waves curled with sounds and with foam, and the invigorating green sea, impregnated with its power, which penetrated all my pores. I see the dark taverns of Callao, where vagabonds from every corner of the planet, we drank Pisco aguardiente as if it were a cautery for bleeding wounds. More people pass, the pretty girls, the matrons with eyes moistened by tenderness, the cordial friends, and the bitterness of a life that will not return assails me. I see the military parades accompanied by sad, monotonous music, which swell my breast with Peruvian patriotism, a patriotism which I interpreted as the affirmation

o: del derecho divino que asiste a las razas nobles y dulces para perpetuarse en un sitio y hacer un oasis de bondad en el vasto mundo perverso. Recuerdo muchas cosas más, y las comparo con las noticias que ahora llegan de allá, y desde el fondo del alma maldigo a quien quiera que haya hecho o esté haciendo sufrir al Perú. Y me digo que no es gobierno honrado el que mutila la patria, haciendo deportar a sus hijos. Los honrados y los fuertes no temen y por lo mismo, no persiguen; en cambio, los que padecen terror aterrorizan. Y les repito que sin libertad y sin justicia ningún gobierno puede ser, ya no digo bueno, tolerable siquiera. Pero los malos gobiernos no dependen del ca. pricho de un hombre, sino del estado de corrupción general de una sociedad. Los tiranos se producen cuando falta una clase independiente y fuerte, es decir, virtuosa. En la actualidad no hay nada que esperar de las clases altas porque pudiendo vivir cómodamente en cualquier parte no necesi. tan sacrificarse, y emigran sin oponer resistencia a la tiranía. Esas clases acomodadas que en la antigua burguesía francesa pudieron ser un baluarte de las libertades públicas, ya no representan ahora ni ese papel útil, y lo único que con ella debe hacerse es reducir sus privilegios mediante una legislación radical. En cambio, la esperanza de los tiempos actuales se encuentra en el elemento trabajador, entendiendo como tal, el conjunto de los que se esfuerzan para ganar el pan en todos los órdenes de las actividades sociales. La clase productora necesita hacerse del poder para socializar la riqueza, y organizar bajo nuevas bases las libertades públicas. El error de los políticos de países donde no ha prendido una revolución, ha sido confiar en la acción de personajes encumbrados, en vez de remover las mayorías trabajado. ras. Recuerdo que, por ejemplo, cuando yo estaba en Lima, mucha gente ilustrada y joven, puso sus esperanzas en un
e: of the divine right that assists noble and gentle races to perpetuate themselves in one place and make an oasis of goodness in the vast perverse world. I recall many things more, and I compare them with the news that now comes from there, and from the bottom of my soul I curse whoever has made or is making Peru suffer. And I tell myself that it is no honest government that mutilates the fatherland by having its sons deported. The honest and the strong do not fear and therefore do not persecute; whereas those who suffer terror terrorise. And I repeat to you that without liberty and without justice no government can be, I do not say good, but even tolerable. But bad governments do not depend on the caprice of one man, but on the state of general corruption of a society. Tyrants are produced when an independent and strong class, that is to say a virtuous one, is lacking. At present there is nothing to expect from the upper classes because, being able to live comfortably anywhere, they need not sacrifice themselves, and they emigrate without opposing resistance to tyranny. Those comfortable classes which in the old French bourgeoisie could be a bulwark of public liberties no longer represent even that useful role now, and the only thing that should be done with them is to reduce their privileges by means of radical legislation. On the other hand, the hope of the present times is found in the working element, understanding by that the whole of those who strive to earn their bread in all the orders of social activity. The producing class needs to take power in order to socialise wealth, and to organise public liberties on new foundations. The error of the politicians of countries where no revolution has taken hold has been to trust in the action of eminent personages instead of stirring the working majorities. I recall, for example, that when I was in Lima, many enlightened and young people placed their hopes in a

o: partido de intelectuales selectos y de señores ricos; un partido de mesas directivas sin contacto alguno con las clases humildes y por lo mismo, cuando vinieron las persecuciones el pueblo no se interesó por defenderlo. Los intelectuales sacrificados clamaron y siguen clamando en el extranjero, pero nadie los escucha, porque ellos no tuvieron en cuenta al pueblo en sus planes. Recuerdo que en aquella época, de mera política hablando en cierta ocasión con un líder de uno de los partidos militantes le dije - abusando un poco de su benevolencia- «¿por qué no suprimen ustedes un partido y con el dinero ahorrado, limpian o canalizan el río?» En efecto, ni se pensaba en pavimentar calles, en sanear barrios, en carreteras y escuelas. Desgraciadamente, así pasa en todos nuestros países, no obstante que todo está por hacer. Por supuesto, obras de verdadera importancia social no puede ejecutarlas un tirano. Un tirano es capaz de abrir avenidas para ponerle su nombre, pero las empresas útiles y silenciosas de la civilización, sólo las realizan los pueblos en masa; no son producto de un hombre, sino de unn generación que ha podido vivir laboriosa y libre. Señalo estas circunstancias simplemente como un ejemplo de la incompetencia de nuestros políticos. Se habla, se discute, se combate, pero rara vez, casi nunca, se construye. Y lo que necesitamos es una política de trabajo, con libertad sin duda, y con justicia social, pero con ardiente vocación de trabajo. Tenemos un atraso de más de cien años respecto al resto del mundo y sólo podríamos reparar lo perdido trabajando doble de todas las demás naciones, trabajando sin descanso, hasta que toda una generación se agote por entero en la obra modesta de alcanzar el nivel de los países civilizados. Nuestra cultura la tenemos en la mente, pero no parece por ninguna parte en la realidad. En el Perú, en México y en Chile, son los extranjeros los que hacen los ferrocarriles, los
e: party of select intellectuals and wealthy gentlemen; a party of executive boards without any contact with the humble classes, and therefore, when the persecutions came, the people took no interest in defending it. The sacrificed intellectuals cried out and go on crying out abroad, but no one listens to them, because they did not take the people into account in their plans. I recall that at that time, speaking of mere politics on a certain occasion with a leader of one of the militant parties, I said to him — abusing his benevolence a little — “why do you not suppress one party and with the money saved clean or channel the river?” Indeed, there was no thought of paving streets, of making districts sanitary, of roads and schools. Unfortunately, so it goes in all our countries, although everything remains to be done. Of course, works of true social importance cannot be carried out by a tyrant. A tyrant is capable of opening avenues to put his name on them, but the useful and silent enterprises of civilisation are accomplished only by peoples in the mass; they are not the product of one man, but of a generation that has been able to live laborious and free. I point to these circumstances simply as an example of the incompetence of our politicians. There is talk, discussion, combat, but rarely, almost never, is anything built. And what we need is a politics of work, with liberty no doubt, and with social justice, but with an ardent vocation for work. We are more than a hundred years behind the rest of the world and could make good what has been lost only by working double the rest of the nations, working without rest, until a whole generation exhausts itself entirely in the modest task of reaching the level of the civilised countries. Our culture we have in the mind, but it does not appear anywhere in reality. In Peru, in Mexico and in Chile, it is foreigners who build the railways, the

o: puentes, los que explotan las minas, los que regentean las grandes empresas y los criollos vivimos de la política o de la explotación usuraria de la tierra o de la miseria burocrática de los puestos del gobierno. Por eso no hemos llegado a constituir verdaderas naciones independientes, sino soberanías ficticias que dan pretexto para holgar veinte o treinta días del año en conmemoraciones de batallas estériles o de planes bastardos. De esta suerte, los mismos sucesos his. tóricos que forman la tradición nacional se van empequeñeciendo aunque sean grandes se van empañando, porque ningún suceso humano merece el recuerdo si no ha sido fecundo, si no ha dado lugar a grandes desenvolvimientos na. cionales o morales. Y nuestros propios fracasos deslustran así las grandes acciones de los fundadores de nuestras nacionalidades. Tenemos vanidad, pero carecemos de orgullo; nos creemos lo mejor del mundo, pero no nos abochorna vi vir como parásitos de una patria donde es el extranjero el que explota las riquezas naturales, el que trabaja y constru ye. Descontentos del valer propio, no podemos llegar a constituir un pueblo, y nos dedicamos a destruirnos, de palabra y de obra. En todas nuestras acciones se revela el desprecio de cada casta contra las otras veinte en que estamos divididos. La casta indostánica tiene una tradición venerable y se funda al fin y al cabo, en diferencias de orden espiritual; pero las castas de la América Latina se basan simplemente en la posesión o carencia de fortuna personal y no por eso la la división es menos honda. En el Perú se habla del huacha. fo, en Chile del roto, en el México pre-rrevolucionario se hablaba despectivamente del pelado. Pero en México, la Revolución puso al pelado, al hombre de campo, al humilde en condiciones de azotar el rostro del hacendado (gamonal) y de dictarle la ley; y si no se suprimen radicalmente la explotación y el abuso, el odio perdura y una nación dividida
e: bridges, who exploit the mines, who manage the great enterprises, and we creoles live from politics or from the usurious exploitation of the land or from the bureaucratic misery of government posts. For that reason we have not come to constitute true independent nations, but fictitious sovereignties that give pretext for idling twenty or thirty days of the year in commemorations of sterile battles or of bastard plans. In this way the very historical events that form the national tradition keep on being belittled, even if they are great, keep on being tarnished, because no human event deserves remembrance if it has not been fruitful, if it has not given rise to great national or moral developments. And our own failures thus dull the great actions of the founders of our nationalities. We have vanity, but we lack pride; we believe ourselves the best in the world, but it does not shame us to live as parasites of a fatherland where it is the foreigner who exploits the natural riches, who works and builds. Discontented with our own worth, we cannot come to constitute a people, and we devote ourselves to destroying one another, in word and deed. In all our actions the contempt of each caste for the other twenty into which we are divided is revealed. The Hindu caste has a venerable tradition and is founded, in the end, on differences of a spiritual order; but the castes of Latin America are based simply on the possession or lack of personal fortune, and the division is no less deep for that. In Peru they speak of the huachafo, in Chile of the roto, in pre-revolutionary Mexico they spoke contemptuously of the pelado. But in Mexico the Revolution put the pelado, the man of the countryside, the humble man, in a position to lash the face of the hacendado (gamonal) and to dictate the law to him; and if exploitation and abuse are not radically suppressed, hatred endures and a divided nation

o: no puede defenderse de sus enemigos exteriores, ni de sus enemigos internos. Los tiranos se sostienen adulando hoy a una casta, mañana a otra; pero sólo cuando desaparecen las castas, se establece la democracia que derriba definitivamente al tirano. Si deseamos aniquilar la tiranía, no en una cabeza, sino en todas sus monstruosas reapariciones, procuremos redimir al indio, al cholo, al huachafo, a todas las gentes que habitan el territorio de su nación. Destierren de la conversación misma ese desdén, esa constante burla del po. bre huachafo, que a veces trabaja más que sus censores y por lo mismo, sirve mejor a la nación. ⁂ Claro que siempre es un problema resolver si la reforma de un país por la educación de sus masas, puede intentarse desde fuera del gobierno o si es mejor derrocar el mal gobierno para constituir uno que se ocupe seriamente de los problemas nacionales; pero en todo caso será prudente comenzar por lo que está más de acuerdo con las posibilidades del momento. La labor de propaganda, la labor de ejemplo que ustedes desarrollan, tendrá que trascender, y crecerá hasta que se torne invencible. Es una lástima que no se hayan aprovechado los años de libertad para organizar movimientos cívicos de carácter educativo; pero ya que se perdió esa ocasión, conviene que ahora quede bien planteado el problema a fin de conocer los medios de atacarlo. ⁂ Uno de los recursos de tiranos es la exaltación del falso patriotismo. El patriotismo que debiera ser siempre amor;
e: cannot defend itself against its external enemies, nor against its internal ones. Tyrants sustain themselves by flattering one caste today, another tomorrow; but only when the castes disappear is democracy established, which definitively overthrows the tyrant. If we desire to annihilate tyranny, not in one head, but in all its monstrous reappearances, let us seek to redeem the Indian, the cholo, the huachafo, all the people who inhabit the territory of your nation. Banish from conversation itself that disdain, that constant mockery of the poor huachafo, who sometimes works more than his critics and therefore serves the nation better. ⁂ Of course it is always a problem to resolve whether the reform of a country through the education of its masses can be attempted from outside the government or whether it is better to overthrow the bad government in order to constitute one that will seriously occupy itself with the national problems; but in any case it will be prudent to begin with what is most in accord with the possibilities of the moment. The labour of propaganda, the labour of example that you are carrying out, will have to spread, and will grow until it becomes invincible. It is a pity that the years of freedom were not used to organise civic movements of an educational character; but since that opportunity was lost, it is fitting that the problem now be well posed, so that the means of attacking it may be known. ⁂ One of the resources of tyrants is the exaltation of false patriotism. Patriotism, which ought always to be love,

o: el déspota le torna en odio, como para apartar de sí la ira del pueblo dirigiéndola contra sus vecinos, contra sus hermanos. No hay déspata que no se exhiba ante sus siervos como un caudilo de la causa nacional, vengador de los agravios patrios y encarnación viviente del orgullo colectivo. Pero nada hay más triste que ver una patria que fía su destino a un solo hombre, y todavía es peor él, espectáculo de un pueblo que entrega sus libertades al déspota por una mera promesa ilusoria. La patria la encarnan sus hijos, jamás sus verdugos. Y un déspota es peor enemigo que veinte ejércitos extranjeros. La patria nada vale si no significa libertad y jus ticia. El orden y la paz fundan el progreso, pero no pueden rendir fruto si no es a base de libertad y de justicia. Organizar un orden social justo y libre, es más importante que fomentar el odio al extranjero. Por eso me atrevo a deciros aun cuando comprendo lo delicado que es hacerlo pero se los digo como quien cumple un deber, que cada vez que el político hable de la cuestión chilena, debéis desconfiar! Sí, debéis deciros: ¿Por qué ese empeño en derrochar la energía peruana en algo que no es la inmediata regeneración por el trabajo y el saber? ¿Cómo vamos a emprender revanchas, si acaso no se han corregido los vicios que originaron la de. rrota? Acabemos primero con la disención interna, construyamos la patria, aumentemos sus recursos, usemos el temple co lectivo para castigar a los tiranos de adentro, y ya después, libres y poderosos podremos enfrentarnos a tiranos de afuera. Las sirenas podridas del despotismo susurran peligros extraños y cantan patriotismos morbosos; pero en realidad no sucede sino que el déspota quiere soldados para sofocar huelgas, para suprimir protestas, para afianzar su dominio. Más varonil que injuriar al enemigo extranjero que está distante y ya no hace daño, es combatir al dictador que deshonra las tropas de la nación cada vez que hace que le pre.
e: the despot turns into hatred, as if to divert the people's wrath from himself by directing it against their neighbours, against their brothers. There is no despot who does not display himself before his serfs as a chieftain of the national cause, avenger of the nation's wrongs and living incarnation of collective pride. But nothing is sadder than to see a fatherland that entrusts its destiny to a single man, and worse still is the spectacle of a people that hands over its liberties to the despot for a mere illusory promise. The fatherland is embodied by its sons, never by its executioners. And a despot is a worse enemy than twenty foreign armies. The fatherland is worth nothing if it does not mean liberty and justice. Order and peace found progress, but they cannot bear fruit except on the basis of liberty and justice. To organise a just and free social order is more important than to foster hatred of the foreigner. That is why I dare to tell you, even though I understand how delicate it is to do so, but I say it to you as one who fulfils a duty, that every time the politician speaks of the Chilean question, you ought to be distrustful! Yes, you ought to say to yourselves: Why this insistence on squandering Peruvian energy on something that is not immediate regeneration through work and knowledge? How are we to undertake revenges, if the vices that gave rise to the defeat have not been corrected? Let us first be done with internal dissension, let us build the fatherland, let us increase its resources, let us use the collective temper to punish the tyrants within, and only afterwards, free and powerful, shall we be able to face the tyrants without. The rotten sirens of despotism whisper strange dangers and sing morbid patriotisms; but in reality what happens is only that the despot wants soldiers to put down strikes, to suppress protests, to secure his dominion. It is more manly to fight the dictator who dishonours the nation's troops every time he has them present

Against the North Americans they hurled us, the Santa Annas, the Victoriano Huertas, the Carranzas, but each of them took care to secure North American aid or tolerance for his own perverse ends. You they incite against the Chileans, and the Chileans against the Peruvians, almost always for selfish reasons of venal politics; for this reason it is necessary to keep in mind that the enemy of the fatherland is rarely outside; almost always he is found within. The enemy of Latin American progress is the hacendado of Mexico, the gamonal of Peru, the estanciero of Argentina and Chile. The exploiters have no fatherland; but they feign one to bewilder the serfs. They hurl peoples against one another to increase their riches or ranks; but it is time now for the peoples to understand that they are brothers and that they have common interests. The nationalism of Latin America has to pass to the secondary plane of a petty and worn-out provincialism. Patriotism needs reforms; there ought no longer to be Peruvians, nor Mexicans, nor Argentines or Chileans. Only souls of molluscs remain attached to the rock of the fatherland. It must be said bluntly: I disown mine, at the very moment when it presumes to enlarge itself at the expense of other nations or is not disposed to serve and love them fraternally and reciprocally. Nor would I lend myself to spending my love in the sterile hatred of past offences. If someone strikes me and is stronger than I and I cannot answer, I ought not to go lamenting the wrong committed; I shall set myself to strive in silence to be stronger, to be better and to win power that one day will repair the injustice. But I shall always return to myself, because the evil is in myself and so is the remedy. And so the citizen

Hence I feel that the first duty of Chileans and Peruvians is to close for ever the spring of hatreds of that accursed War of the Pacific. Let the pending questions be resolved in haste and in any way whatever, and then curse them all at once, but then forget them, all those fools, blunderers or arrogant men who consummated a war that divided the Iberian stock at the very time when the Anglo-Saxons of the North of the Continent sealed with blood the perennial alliance of the Northern side with the Southern side, thus raising the foundation of North American power. This stain on Ibero-Americanism, which is called the War of the Pacific, can be erased only by the two youths of Peru and Chile. And when the moment comes, do not dispute territories; leave the land to whoever makes the best use of it, to whoever needs it most; but, that above all, take care not to leave standing a single monument that recalls the crime; pull down the statues, efface the inscriptions, chastise history, and let not a single memory remain of the accursed dispute that poisons the soul of two noble peoples. Workers or thinkers of the two rival countries, only you, who work or who think, can turn hatred into love and strife into progress. And for this no tyrants are needed; they are in the way. ⁂ ⁂ The present situation of Peru is painful and bitter, all the more so because it is not exceptional, but one of those intermittent calamities from which it is very hard to free oneself. We have passed through similar shames and are threatened with suffering them again. Experience ought by now to convince us that the remedy has to be a collective remedy of general education and common action. Organise

It will be said to me that it is very difficult to shake majorities who attend only to their immediate and material interests; but it is also true that every reform begins with the action of an intrepid minority, which, if it is in the right and is tenacious, ends by imposing itself on everything. There is not a single case of an honest and resolute youth that has not made itself heir to command. The secret is to persevere in a noble and lofty purpose. Be firmer, more tenacious than your enemies: more sober, more industrious, clearer in thought and more resolute in action, and triumph will come unexpected and splendid. And as soon as you have conquered, as soon as all Peru is in your hands, make it lovable again, make it sweet again; but before all else, make it just, so that kindness and sweetness may be true and lasting. Viendo tan corto lo que hoy se alcanza, nos consuela mirar hacia los que pueden empujar el ideal, así que nosotros caigamos vencidos. Nadie puede explicar qué es lo que vienen hacer sobre esta tierra maldita, los millares de seres que nacen a diario para padecer y morir sin dejar huella. Las teorías de la vida como redención parecían irrefutables cuando el pensamiento se encerraba en la tribu y se creía que el ciclo de la existencia planetaria abarcaba unos cuantos siglos, desde el génesis hasta el juicio final; pero de entonces a la fecha, el espíritu humano ha creado otra Biblia en el conocimiento científico, fundado en el raciocinio, la observación y la experiencia, fuentes también divinas de sabiduría, y esta nue. va Biblia nos habla de un planeta que ha tardado miles, acaso millones de años, en constituirse y de una sucesión de
e: Addressed to Germán Arciniegas] Dear Sir and Friend: I have received your letter of last April in which you inform me of the approaching celebration of a Congress of Colombian youth, and ask me for a few words for the occasion. Your letter has moved me not only because you have remembered me, but because the children of this combative age often feel the need to rest our longing upon those who are to replace us tomorrow. Seeing how little is attained today, it consoles us to look toward those who can push the ideal forward once we have fallen vanquished. No one can explain what it is that they come to do upon this accursed earth, the thousands of beings who are born daily to suffer and die without leaving a trace. The theories of life as redemption seemed irrefutable when thought was shut up within the tribe and it was believed that the cycle of planetary existence embraced a few centuries, from the genesis to the last judgement; but since then, the human spirit has created another Bible in scientific knowledge, founded on reasoning, observation and experience, also divine sources of wisdom, and this new Bible speaks to us of a planet that has taken thousands, perhaps millions of years to form, and of a succession of

o: especies y dé seres, entre los cuales aparecemos nosotros co. mo un instante asombroso, que fulgura brevemente para rodar en el abismo de los milenios. Ante esta concepción absurda y basta ¿que hemos de hacer sino aprovechar nuestro instante para ensancharlo en toda la plenitud de los tiempos; para prolongarlo, ya que es tan corto en toda la extensión infinita? ⁂ ⁂ Todos vemos, unos confusamente, otros con clarividencia, que somos arrastrados por una corriente sombría que se ilumina a ratos con fulgor, como de intuición divina. Lo. grar estos instantes de iluminación, en que adivinamos una manera de escapar del ciclo absurdo, tal es la potencialidad más alta de nuestra naturaleza y el fin supremo de la vida: Pero si hemos de ejercitar nuestra conciencia, ya sea para este objeto o para otro cualquiera, es necesario romper la modorra del cuerpo y la estupidez del ambiente. Para que el cuerpo no moleste se le satisface; para que el trabajo no robe toda nuestra energía se perfecciona nuestro dominio sobre la naturaleza, obligándola a que rinda frutos con poco esfuerzo; y para que la vida social se convierta en una colaboradora del espíritu, hay que reformarla a base de franqueza y de justicia, franqueza que descubre la realidad hasta lo más recóndito y justicia derivada, no de las leyes que son fruto de las argucias de la mente, sino de la ley superior del corazón. De esta suerte, produciendo riqueza con el trabajo y repartiendo los bienes con equidad, se logrará que todos puedan dar su mendrugo al cuerpo, sin necesidad de vender el tesoro mayor del alma, que es el tiempo. La maldición de la vida colectiva resulta del contraste de la pereza de los que no trabajan, y la esclavitud de los que trabajan tanto, que el trabajo material les consume la capacidad de la meditación y la alegría. Este es el estado de
e: species and beings, among which we appear as an astonishing instant, which flashes briefly only to roll into the abyss of the millennia. Before this absurd and coarse conception, what are we to do but make use of our instant in order to widen it to the whole fullness of the ages; to prolong it, since it is so short, over the whole infinite extension? ⁂ ⁂ We all see, some confusedly, others with clairvoyance, that we are dragged along by a sombre current which is lit at times with a gleam, as of divine intuition. To achieve these instants of illumination, in which we divine a way of escaping from the absurd cycle, such is the highest potentiality of our nature and the supreme end of life: But if we are to exercise our consciousness, whether for this object or for any other, it is necessary to break the drowsiness of the body and the stupidity of the environment. That the body may not trouble us it is satisfied; that work may not rob us of all our energy we perfect our dominion over nature, obliging it to yield fruits with little effort; and that social life may become a collaborator of the spirit, it must be reformed on the basis of frankness and justice, a frankness that uncovers reality down to its most recondite part, and a justice derived not from laws, which are the fruit of the quibbles of the mind, but from the higher law of the heart. In this way, producing wealth by work and distributing goods with equity, it will be achieved that all can give their crust to the body, without need of selling the greater treasure of the soul, which is time. The curse of collective life results from the contrast between the laziness of those who do not work and the slavery of those who work so much that material labour consumes their capacity for meditation and joy. Desde que Tolstoi acabó con el mito del génio como caudillo ya no buscan los pueblos ídolos que ensalzar, sino injusticias que corregir. El Quijote triunfa en el mundo; pero ha aprendido mucho en estos siglos de fracasos, y ahora ya no es el loco que mueve a risa, sino el caballero de la fuerza, al servicio de la generosidad y de la inteligencia. El génio para nosotros no es el que arrebata para sí gloria o poder, sino el que derrocha saber o energía. Y nuestra época toda, quiere que sea universal, todo lo que ha sido exclusivo: la dicha, el saber, el poder…… Queremos además, que lo excelso se cumpla no sólo allá arriba, sino tambiéu aquí abajo, y tachamos de impostor a todo el que levanta, impotente, las manos al cielo, en vez de usar los puños para corregir la injusticia…. ¿Pero dónde va a estar el centro de esta palingenesia próxima, a la vez humana y divina?… Los europeos con el pretexto de ambiciones nacionalistas, pero en realidad porque se han producido con exceso, seguirán destrozándose hasta que las matanzas y la emigración descongestionen de habitantes una tierra que llegó a dar más bocas que panes. Víctimas de una organización errada, no podrán enseñarnos; se limitarán á invadirnos, proporcionándonos la sávia de una humanidad nueva. La mezcla libre de razas y culturas, reproducirá en mayor escala y con mejores elementos, el ensayo de universalismo que fracasó en Norteamérica. Allí fracasó porque se volvió norteamericanismo; aquí puede salvarse si la ductibilidad y la fuerza ibéricas ponen la base de un tipo realmente universal. La conciencia de es la misión late en todos los pueblos de la América Latina, y da impulso al latinoamericanismo contemporáneo. Un moderno latinoamericanismo de Bolivar, porque el de entonces era un sueño político, en tanto que el de ahora es étnico. Bolívar quería una Liga de Naciones Americanas, que no
e: barbarism in which the world has lived up to now, but precisely our age is characterised by a longing for universal redemption and for happiness for all, without hypocrisies and without pretences. Since Tolstoy put an end to the myth of the genius as chieftain, peoples no longer seek idols to extol, but injustices to correct. Quixote triumphs in the world; but he has learned much in these centuries of failures, and now he is no longer the madman who moves to laughter, but the knight of strength, at the service of generosity and of intelligence. The genius for us is not he who snatches glory or power for himself, but he who lavishes knowledge or energy. And our whole age wants everything that has been exclusive to be universal: happiness, knowledge, power…… We want, moreover, that the exalted be fulfilled not only up there, but also down here, and we brand as an impostor everyone who raises his hands to heaven, impotent, instead of using his fists to correct injustice…. But where is the centre of this approaching palingenesis, at once human and divine, to be?… The Europeans, under the pretext of nationalist ambitions, but in reality because they have multiplied to excess, will go on tearing one another to pieces until the slaughters and emigration relieve of inhabitants a land that came to yield more mouths than loaves. Victims of an erring organisation, they will not be able to teach us; they will limit themselves to invading us, supplying us with the sap of a new humanity. The free mixture of races and cultures will reproduce, on a larger scale and with better elements, the experiment in universalism that failed in North America. There it failed because it turned into North Americanism; here it can be saved if Iberian ductility and strength lay the basis of a truly universal type. The consciousness of this mission throbs in all the peoples of Latin America, and gives impulse to contemporary Latin Americanism. A modern Latin Americanism of Bolívar, because that of his day was a political dream, whereas that of today is ethnic. Bolívar wanted a League of American Nations, which did not

Nosotros queremos la union de los pueblos ibéricos, sin excluir a España y comprendiendo expresamente al Brasil; y tenemos que excluir a los Estados Unidos, no por odio, sino porque ellos representan otra expresión de la historia humana, Bolívar interpretando en grande las ideas de su tiempo, quiso una liga de Naciones Americanas, capaz de garantizar la libertad de todo el mundo. ⁂ Esto mismo volvió a expresarlo, con menos grandeza, cien años más tarde, el doctrinarismo mediocre de Wodrow Wilson, cuando excitaba a las naciones americanas, para que participasen en la guerra europea, con el fin de garantizar la «democracia en el mundo. A Bolívar no se le oyó porque no había llegado la hora; pero su ideal renace más preciso y más fuerte. A Wilson no se le escuchó porqué los países ibéricos saben lo que es la democracia en el país del dolar, y tienen su propio ideal no meramente político, sino más bien místico, de dar expresión a cada raza conforme a su misión y su temperamento. Creemos que es más importante para una raza, conservar su idiosincracia que su territorio, y por eso exigimos la emancipación espiritual por en
e: exclude the United States of the North. We want the union of the Iberian peoples, without excluding Spain and expressly including Brazil; and we have to exclude the United States, not out of hatred, but because they represent another expression of human history. Bolívar, interpreting on a grand scale the ideas of his time, wanted a league of American Nations, capable of guaranteeing the liberty of the whole world. ⁂ This same thing was expressed again, with less grandeur, a hundred years later, by the mediocre doctrinairism of Woodrow Wilson, when he urged the American nations to take part in the European war, in order to guarantee "democracy in the world." Bolívar was not heard because the hour had not come; but his ideal is reborn more precise and stronger. Wilson was not listened to because the Iberian countries know what democracy is in the land of the dollar, and have their own ideal, not merely political but rather mystical, of giving expression to each race according to its mission and temperament. Within the most generous internationalism and loyally recognising the universal capacity of men, we nevertheless want peoples not to be despoiled of their own spiritual characters, because each of them is like a distinct road for the revelation of the divine and no one has the right to suppress a single one of these roads. We believe that it is more important for a race to preserve its idiosyncrasy than its territory, and for that reason we demand spiritual emancipation above

o: cima de la política. En este punto, Bolívar no podía pensar como nosotros; acababa de sacudir el yugo español y llevado de un exceso natural de sentimiento, se inclinaba á simpatizar con el inglés, el ancestral enemigo de España y de la raza española ; en cambio, ahora sentimos, que vuelve a ser nuestro enemigo el que lo sea de España. Este retorno al sentido común ha sido muy lento, a tal grado, que todavía algunos pueblos de nuestro Continente, se ufanan de guerreros de la independencia que eran irlandeses o escoceses, héroes y todo, pero al fin súbditos británicos, que peleaban de paso por el país americano, pero en realidad por atavismo de estirpe y porque liberando a la América Española, se debilitaba a España y se agrandaba Inglaterra. La confusión de sentimientos no tiene nada de extraño, pues mal podemos depurar la historia, cuando nuestras mismas ideas no han estado enteramente claras. ⁂ ⁂ A raiz de nuestra independencia nos salieron tutores, y la presión mental de Francia sirvió, como ha servido casi siempre, en la historia, para debilitar a los latinos y asegurar el triunfo de los ingleses. El nacionalismo francés, torpemente imitado, nos llevó a constituir patrias ajenas, unas de otras, y sin darnos cuenta, reemplazamos todo lo que tiene de más firme un pueblo, su tradición noble, sus parentescos raciales, su unidad histórica, por la vana palabrería importada con etiquetas extrañas. Así nos disgregamos - hipnotizados con la primer tontería llegada de París-,y todo esto lo hacíamos mientras la raza sajona, llevada de un sabio instinto, se organizaba para constituir el «english speaking world» contemporáneo, dominador del planeta. El intento de conquista hecho por los ingleses en la Argentina y las usurpaciones de territorios consumados en Venezuela, (en México, etc., sirvieron para recordarros el
e: politics. On this point, Bolívar could not think as we do; he had just shaken off the Spanish yoke and, carried away by a natural excess of feeling, he was inclined to sympathise with the Englishman, the ancestral enemy of Spain and of the Spanish race; we, on the other hand, now feel that whoever is the enemy of Spain becomes again our enemy. This return to common sense has been very slow, to such a degree that some peoples of our Continent still pride themselves on warriors of independence who were Irishmen or Scotsmen, heroes and all, but in the end British subjects, who fought in passing for the American country, but in reality by atavism of stock and because by liberating Spanish America, Spain was weakened and England enlarged. The confusion of feelings is nothing strange, for we can hardly purify history when our own ideas have not been entirely clear. ⁂ ⁂ In the wake of our independence guardians sprang up for us, and the mental pressure of France served, as it has almost always served in history, to weaken the Latins and to assure the triumph of the English. French nationalism, clumsily imitated, led us to constitute fatherlands alien to one another, and without realising it, we replaced all that is firmest in a people, its noble tradition, its racial kinships, its historical unity, with vain verbiage imported under foreign labels. Thus we broke up -- hypnotised by the first piece of nonsense that arrived from Paris --, and all this we were doing while the Saxon race, led by a wise instinct, was organising itself to constitute the contemporary "english speaking world," master of the planet. The attempt at conquest made by the English in Argentina and the usurpations of territory consummated in Venezuela, (in Mexico, etc., served to remind us of the

o: peligro. Los cinco o seis mil ingleses aniquilados totalmente en Buenos Aires, nos hicieron ver que la patria no es un sólo territorio y la libertad política, sino también y principalmente la estirpe, es decir, el tipo de cultura a que ca. da pueblo pertenece. La mera nacionalidad se forja en papeles; la estirpe la constituye la vida. La creación de las nacionalidades latinoamericanas la constituye la vida. La creación de las nacionalidades latinoamericanas fué un caso de suicidio colectivo. Bolívar lo comprendió, y para evitarlo empleó todos los recursos de su enorme ingenio; sin embargo, el egoísmo, las barreras naturales y el interés de las potencias extrañas fueron más fuertes. El interés de Inglaterra prefirió veinte clientes a uno sólo. La vanidad de Francia no podía ver bien un gran pueblo delante del cual hubiera parecido la maestra un poco ridícula, pero consintió en mostrar cierta desdeñosa condescendencia, para los veinte discípulos, como nosotros mismos dimos en llamarnos. Nos llegó todo lo extraño; los ingleses se apoderaron de nuestro mercados, regalándonos teorías conforme a las cuales ellos son la raza superior y nosotros unos mestizos,capaces tal vez de aprender, pero mediante la obediencia y la imitación. Los franceses nos llenaron de cosas bonitas y llegaban a la Argentina para decir que aquel era el mejor país de la América, porque se hallaba más cerca culturalmente de Francia, y en seguida permitían que el peruano se afrancesara, como discípulo predilecto para gloriarse a renglón seguido, de que todavía era más francés el Brasil; y todos estabamos de acuerdo en que…. el cerebro del mundo estaba en Paris. The five or six thousand Englishmen totally annihilated in Buenos Aires made us see that the fatherland is not merely a territory and political liberty, but also and principally the stock, that is, the type of culture to which each people belongs. Mere nationality is forged on paper; the stock is constituted by life. The creation of the Latin American nationalities is constituted by life. The creation of the Latin American nationalities was a case of collective suicide. Bolívar understood it, and to avoid it employed all the resources of his enormous ingenuity; nevertheless, egoism, natural barriers and the interest of foreign powers were stronger. The interest of England preferred twenty clients to a single one. The vanity of France could not look kindly on a great people before which the teacher would have seemed a little ridiculous, but it consented to show a certain disdainful condescension toward the twenty disciples, as we ourselves took to calling ourselves. Everything foreign reached us; the English took possession of our markets, presenting us with theories according to which they are the superior race and we are mestizos, perhaps capable of learning, but by way of obedience and imitation. The French filled us with pretty things and arrived in Argentina to say that it was the best country in America, because it stood nearer culturally to France, and straightway allowed the Peruvian to become Frenchified, as a favourite disciple, to boast in the next breath that Brazil was still more French; and we were all agreed that .... the brain of the world was in Paris. The French, for their part, held in agreement that the brain of the world was in Paris. The French, for their part, held in agreement that the Latin American was a poor wretch. And they were right; we handed over our riches and we handed over our soul, and like good renegades we

Países de opereta trágica; razas bastar. das, hemos sido los simios del mundo, porque habiendo renegado decasi todo lo propio, nos pusimos a imitar sin fé y sin esperanza de crear. e: did nothing but insult Spain, puffed up with pride in our new masters, for masters they were even in the protection or tolerance they always lent to the despots who knew how to favour their interests. Look at the Venezuela of today, fief of the last and most monstrous of tyrants, protégé of the foreign companies that exploit the country, and you will see as in a mirror what in different epochs Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala and Mexico were. Our independence was on paper, and our decorum in the mire. Countries of tragic operetta; bastard races, we have been the apes of the world, because having disowned almost everything of our own, we set ourselves to imitate without faith and without hope of creating. The war waged by Juárez against the French began the regeneration of Mexico; other, more fortunate countries have been regenerating themselves by the orderly effort of their own development, and we have at last arrived at the decisive period in which we live, to hear that from one end to the other the Bolivarian concept arises renewed, but now much more profound because it no longer seeks the political league for abstract ends, but the integration of a race, which arrives at the instant of its universal mission. Fortunate the Latin American youth that comes to life when the foundations of a new period in the history of the world are being laid! But how much tenacity and clairvoyance it is going to need so that the whirlwind of events may not blind it and so that those who have come from outside may not displace it from its role as interpreter of the foreign contribution and unifier of human creation! It needs to cleanse the environment so that the new life may develop vigorous and free; it needs to be done with the soldier and the cleric, so that it may not again be foreign influences that liberate. It needs to implant justice so that here a new barbarism may not be produced, but a true civilisation. ⁂ Those who look only backward, those who compromise with injustice and with lying will not be able to handle the human material that is about to overflow upon us. If youth
