e: necessary, first, to wrest the power of the landlords in order to place it in the hands of the people. When some of our enemies proclaim us Bolsheviks, we can always answer with the facts: "In reality we are a feudal State that is trying to modernise itself." In truth we are trying to implant an agrarian regime similar to that which exists in Ohio, in New England or in the Dakotas. And if Kansas, with its thousands of fertile farms, is Bolshevik, then we too wish to be so. Returning to the educational matter, I shall say that we are endeavouring to transform the environment that surrounds us so that it may produce better men; we are changing the agrarian regime in order to have, not simply inhabitants, but citizens and men. And I do not hesitate to affirm that the basis of our educational system lies in a better distribution of property and of the products of labour. A just solution of the economic problem is the first step of educational reform. Yes, our aim is, as I have defined it before, to create free men and not slaves. The Revolution, transformed into government, is engaged in solving the economic problems of the country. The people elect their officials and make their own laws; the average of the people's material well-being has noticeably improved; nevertheless our progress is slow because we work amid the ruins and the errors of centuries of bad government and of the last ten years of war. In spite of this, a powerful moral current keeps consciences alert, and it may be affirmed that everyone realises the demands of the moment and prepares to fulfil his duty. Thus it is explained that people who had almost forgotten the

o: deberes del Estado, por lo que hace a educación, presten actualmente todo su apoyo a un gobierno que por la voz del Presidente Obregón, el más distinguido general de la Revolución, ha proclamado la necesidad de licenciar soldados y reclutar maestros de cerrar cuarteles y abrir escuelas. Millares de soldados han regresado ya a la vida civil, y millares de maestros trabajan como soldados del progreso en las ciudades y en los distritos rurales; y aun en las más remotas comarcas indígenas, centenares de misioneros, con carácter oficial, y otros como voluutarios, trabajan entre los ignorantes para enseñarles a leer y escribir, buenas costumbres y métodos de trabajo más eficaces. Estos maestros misioneros preceden el trabajo de la escuela y lo preparan, y ya han logrado despertar el interés de toda la población en favor de la educación pública, Con el objeto de dar mayor impulso a la campaña educacional, fué necesario reformar la Constitución con el fin de crear un Ministerio federal de Educación Pública. Este Ministerio tiene facultades para crear y sostener toda clase de instituciones educativas en cualquiera región del país, colaborando con los Consejos de Educación de los distintos Estados de la Unión, o procediendo independientemente, según sea más coveniente y práctico, El presupuesto de que dispone el Ministerio ha sido, durante el presente año, de algo más de cuarenta y nueve millones de pesos, o sea cerca de veinticuatro millones de dóllares. Para dar una idea de lo que esta cantidad representa entre nosotros, bastará recordar que la mayor suma destinada a educación pública en los tiempos de Porfirio Díaz, es decir, hace solamente doce años, fué de ocho millones de pesos, o sean cuatro millones de dóllares; después Madero aumentó esta suma a doce millones de pesos; pero Carranza la redujo a menos de seis; de modo que el actual Gobierno ha
e: duties of the State with regard to education now lend all their support to a government which, by the voice of President Obregón, the most distinguished general of the Revolution, has proclaimed the necessity of discharging soldiers and recruiting teachers, of closing barracks and opening schools. Thousands of soldiers have already returned to civil life, and thousands of teachers work as soldiers of progress in the cities and in the rural districts; and even in the most remote Indian regions, hundreds of missionaries, with official character, and others as volunteers, work among the ignorant to teach them to read and write, good habits and more efficient methods of work. These missionary teachers precede the work of the school and prepare it, and have already succeeded in awakening the interest of the whole population in favour of public education. In order to give greater impetus to the educational campaign, it was necessary to reform the Constitution so as to create a federal Ministry of Public Education. This Ministry has power to create and maintain every kind of educational institution in any region of the country, collaborating with the Councils of Education of the various States of the Union, or proceeding independently, as may be more convenient and practical. The budget at the disposal of the Ministry has been, during the present year, somewhat more than forty-nine million pesos, that is, nearly twenty-four million dollars. To give an idea of what this amount represents among us, it will suffice to recall that the largest sum allotted to public education in the times of Porfirio Díaz, that is, only twelve years ago, was eight million pesos, or four million dollars; afterwards Madero increased this sum to twelve million pesos; but Carranza reduced it to less than six; so that the present Government has

o: subido el gasto de poco menos de seis millones que pagaba Carranza a los cuarenta y nueve del presupuesto actual. Por supuesto los gobiernos locales, hoy como antes, continúan dedicando sumas anuales para el sostenimiento de sus propias escuelas, celebrándose cada año los convenios correspondientes para asegurar la colaboración de las autoridades federales y las locales en materias escolares. Los sueldos de los maestros se han duplicado y en muchos casos triplicado, habiéndose logrado establecer el salario mínimo de tres pesos diarios para cada maestro, no obstante que el mínimo anterior era, a veces, menor de un peso por día. Al mismo tiempo se ha tratado de fortalecer el decoro de los maestros y el sentimiento de su propia responsabilidad, concediéndoles, en la generalidad de los casos, el derecho de elegir candidatos para las jefaturas de departamentos y dirección de escuelas; pues hemos juzgado que si nos hemos dedicado a educar hombres libres, debemos empezar por hacer maestros libres. Lo que equivale a decir: páguese a los maestros lo más que sea posible y permítaseles que se organicen según su propio saber y experiencia; un saber y experiencia que será superior, por lo menos, al criterio del político o de los Consejos Ejecutivos que en otras partes manejan los colegios. Junto con la necesidad de mejorar las condiciones econó. micas y sociales de los maestros, hemos tenido que afrontar el problema de las necesidades del niño. Naturalmente no nos hemos preocupado mucho por los hijos de los ricos, puesto que sus padres pueden atenderlos, y el deber del Estado consiste en ayudar a los que lo necesiten, mostrándoles preferencia. e: raised the expenditure from the little less than six millions that Carranza paid to the forty-nine of the present budget. Of course the local governments, today as before, continue to devote annual sums to the maintenance of their own schools, the corresponding agreements being made every year to ensure the collaboration of the federal and the local authorities in school matters. The salaries of the teachers have been doubled and in many cases tripled, the minimum wage of three pesos a day for each teacher having been established, although the previous minimum was at times less than one peso a day. At the same time an effort has been made to strengthen the dignity of the teachers and the feeling of their own responsibility, granting them, in the generality of cases, the right to elect candidates for the heads of departments and the direction of schools; for we have judged that if we have devoted ourselves to educating free men, we must begin by making free teachers. Which is equivalent to saying: let the teachers be paid as much as is possible and let them be permitted to organise themselves according to their own knowledge and experience; a knowledge and experience that will be superior, at the least, to the judgement of the politician or of the Executive Councils that elsewhere manage the colleges. Together with the need to improve the economic and social conditions of the teachers, we have had to face the problem of the needs of the child. Naturally we have not worried much about the children of the rich, since their parents can look after them, and the duty of the State consists in helping those who need it, showing them preference. Our former educational institutions,

o: aunque limitadas en número, se hallaban perfectamente or ganizadas conforme a los más modernos métodos pedagógicos; pero en nuestro esfuerzo de reconstrucción la reali. dad nos ha obligado a hacer a un lado un sinnúmero de bellas teorías. Por ejemplo: teníamos escuelas de niños anormales en las que se practicaban exámenes cuidadosos, anotados en registros que después servían para formar conclusiones generales más o menos triviales. Tuvimos que acabar con estos lujos de dudosa utilidad inmediata, y con excepción, por supuesto, de los sordomudos y ciegos, qus asisten a planteles especiales, reunimos a todos los niños en el mismo tipo de escuela primaria, y en todas ellas establecimos el desayuno escolar, gratuito para los pobres. De esta manera, lo que ahorramos en médicos lo gastamos en pan; la experiencia nos ha demostrado que una buena ración matinal es mucho más eficaz que el médico para curar la deblidad del carácter y la lentitud del pensamiento. Subsiste, por supues. to, el servicio médico, que practica visitas periódicas a las escuelas; pero tratamos de hacer comprender a los médicos que no nos importa mucho que aconsejen a los niños ni que nos remitan largos informes escritos, sino que la Nación les paga para que curen. El médico, antiguamente, se ocupaba en recetar drogas que, en la generalidad de los casos, el niño no podía comprar: hoy aplica directamente el tratamiento, y el resultado es que estamos a punto de desterrar las enfermedades de la piel, que antes se consideró imposible combatir dentro de la escuela. Nuestro servicio dental gratuito se está extendiendo a todas las escuelas, y, a medida que disponemos de fondos, establecemos en cada escuela, también gratuitamente, baños, estanques de natación y campos de recreo. En realidad nuestros planes son tan amplios, que acaso sean censurados por pretender abarcar demasiado;
e: though limited in number, were perfectly organised in accordance with the most modern pedagogical methods; but in our effort of reconstruction reality has obliged us to set aside a countless number of beautiful theories. For example: we had schools for abnormal children in which careful examinations were practised, noted in registers that afterwards served to draw general conclusions more or less trivial. We had to put an end to these luxuries of doubtful immediate utility, and with the exception, of course, of the deaf-mutes and the blind, who attend special schools, we gathered all the children into the same type of primary school, and in all of them we established the school breakfast, free for the poor. In this way, what we save on doctors we spend on bread; experience has shown us that a good morning ration is much more effective than the doctor in curing weakness of character and slowness of thought. There remains, of course, the medical service, which makes periodic visits to the schools; but we try to make the doctors understand that it does not matter much to us that they advise the children or send us long written reports, but that the Nation pays them to cure. The doctor, formerly, busied himself in prescribing drugs which, in the generality of cases, the child could not buy: today he applies the treatment directly, and the result is that we are on the point of banishing the diseases of the skin, which before it was thought impossible to combat within the school. Our free dental service is being extended to all the schools, and, as we have funds at our disposal, we establish in each school, also free of charge, baths, swimming pools and playing fields. In reality our plans are so ample that perhaps they may be censured for trying to embrace too much;

o: pero de todas maneras debo hacer constar que los maestros, hombres y mujeres, que participan en nuestra obra, tienen la convicción de que no sólo desempeñan una función cívica, sino que trabajan en una especie de moderna cruzada para la elevación y liberación de los espíritus y el mejoramiento de los cuerpos de sus semejantes; por eso el fervor que ponen en su obra es un fervor religioso, y la recompensa que reciben no está ni en el dinero ni en los ascensos, sino en el sentimiento apostólico, en el goce místico que los anima y sostiene. El gobierno de Díaz estableció algunas buenas escuelas en las principales ciudades — entre ellas varias Normales — para la educación de los maestros. Estas escuelas nos han servido mucho, principalmente porque de ellas hemos tomado
e: but at all events I must put on record that the teachers, men and women, who take part in our work, have the conviction that they not only perform a civic function, but that they labour in a kind of modern crusade for the elevation and liberation of the spirits and the betterment of the bodies of their fellows; for that reason the fervour they put into their work is a religious fervour, and the reward they receive lies neither in money nor in promotions, but in the apostolic feeling, in the mystical enjoyment that animates and sustains them. At first it was a kind of Pythagorean inspiration. What is good, we told ourselves, must answer to number and measure, and in virtue of this we resolved to divide the Ministry into three great branches. Afterwards experience has shown us that we were right. The educational work of the whole country is subdivided in the following manner: First, schools; second, libraries; third, fine arts Primary education, secular and compulsory, was decreed in Mexico more than sixty years ago. Since then parents have been obliged to send their children to school; but in a great many places there have been no schools. The Díaz government established some good schools in the principal cities — among them several Normal schools — for the education of teachers. These schools have served us well, chiefly because from them we have taken

o: el núcleo de maestros hábiles que actualmente utilizamos. El error fundamental que se había cometido era no mandar maestros a los distritos rurales. En la actualidad pagamos mejor sueldo a los que prestan sus servicios en las regiones distantes del país, y procuramos enviar allá lo mejor de nuestro personal. En la escuela elemental se enseña la lectura y la escritura y además, cursos breves de historia, geografía y aritmé tica. También sostenemos un pequeño número de maestros viajeros de trabajos manuales, que visitan los pequeños poblados para enseñar elementos de carpintería, herrería y agricultura. De esta suerte aplicamos el principio que norma nuestra enseñanza desde la escuela elemental hasta la universitaria, y que puede condensarse en lo siguiente: «Enseñanza elemental y educacion técnica». La escuela elemental se establece en las pequeñas ciudades; en los distritos rurales su equivalente se encuentra en la escuela rural. Varias de las regiones más distantes están pobladas por indios que no conocen el castellano; naturalmente empezamos por enseñarles esté idioma, y tan pronto como aprenden pueden pasar a la escuela elemental de tipo ordinario, o a la secundaria y después a la profesional, siempre que llenen los mismos resultados que se exigen del resto de la población. Recientemente se ha escrito mucho acerca de la mejor manera de educar á los indios de pura raza, siendo numerosos los partidarios de la creación de escuelas especiales de indios; pero siempre he sido enemigo de esta medida porque fatalmente conduce al sistema llamado de la reservación», que divide la población en castas y colores de piel, y nosotros deseamos educar al indio para asimilarlo totalmente a nuestra nacionalidad y no para hacerlo a un lado. En realidad creo que debe seguirse, para educar al indio, el método venerable de los grandes educadoros españoles, que como Las Casas, Vasco de Quiroga y Motolinía, adaptaron al indio a la civilización europea, creando de
e: the nucleus of skilled teachers whom we now employ. The fundamental error that had been committed was not to send teachers to the rural districts. At present we pay a better salary to those who serve in the distant regions of the country, and we try to send there the best of our personnel. In the elementary school reading and writing are taught and, besides, short courses in history, geography and arithmetic. We also maintain a small number of travelling teachers of manual trades, who visit the small settlements to teach the elements of carpentry, blacksmithing and agriculture. In this way we apply the principle that governs our teaching from the elementary school to the university, and that can be condensed in the following: "Elementary instruction and technical education." The elementary school is established in the small towns; in the rural districts its equivalent is found in the rural school. Several of the most distant regions are populated by Indians who do not know Castilian; naturally we begin by teaching them this language, and as soon as they learn it they can pass to the elementary school of the ordinary type, or to the secondary school and afterwards to the professional, provided they meet the same requirements that are demanded of the rest of the population. Recently much has been written about the best way of educating the Indians of pure race, and there are numerous partisans of the creation of special schools for Indians; but I have always been an enemy of this measure because it fatally leads to the system called the "reservation," which divides the population into castes and colours of skin, and we wish to educate the Indian in order to assimilate him wholly to our nationality and not to set him aside. In truth I believe that, in order to educate the Indian, we should follow the venerable method of the great Spanish educators, who, like Las Casas, Vasco de Quiroga and Motolinía, adapted the Indian to European civilisation, thus creating

o: esta suerte nuevos países y nuevas razas, en lugar de borrar a los naturales o de reducirlos al aislamiento. No concibo que exista diferencia alguna entre el indio ignorante y el campesino francés ignorante o el campesino inglés ignorante; tau pronto como unos y otros son educados, se convierten en auxiliares de la vida civilizada de sus países, y contribuyen, cada uno en su medida, al mejoramiento del mundo. Por esta razón no he hablado del problema indígena, sino sim. plemente del problema de la ignorancia; ignorancia que se agrava por la indiferencia, y aun, a veces, la crueldad de los que, teniendo educación y riqueza, no hacen nada eficaz en beneficio de sus semejantes, Después de dos años de educación elemental, tenemos lá escuela superior, que abarca cuatro años y, después de los seis años de primaria, el alumno que puede hacerlo pasa a los colegios preparatorios y en seguida a la profesional. colegios preparatorios son más de veinte, situados en diferentes partes del país, siendo el principal el que está agregado a la Universidad Nacional de México; pero el proyecto de la Secretaría de Educación es concentrar sus esfuerzos en las cuatro grandes universidades de la ciudad de México, de Guadalajara, de Yucatán y de Monterrey. Sin embargo, aun más urgente que el problema de la universidad, es, para nosotros, la transformación de nuestras antiguas escuelas de artes y oficios en modernos institutos técnicos. En ellos deseamos educar peritos mecánicos, industriales de todo gé nero y trabajadores en las artes de la ciencia aplicada, con la esperanza de reducir, de esta manera, la carga del proletariado profesionista, que constituye entre nosotros una verdadera calamidad pública. A fin, pues, de suprimir el para. sitismo y de aumentar el número de los productos de rique. za, nos proponemos establecer, por lo menos, una escuela técnica moderna en cada uno de los granndes centros de población.
e: new countries and new races, instead of wiping out the natives or reducing them to isolation. I cannot conceive that there is any difference between the ignorant Indian and the ignorant French peasant or the ignorant English peasant; as soon as the one and the other are educated, they become auxiliaries of the civilised life of their countries, and contribute, each in his measure, to the betterment of the world. For this reason I have not spoken of the Indian problem, but simply of the problem of ignorance; an ignorance that is aggravated by the indifference, and even, at times, the cruelty of those who, having education and wealth, do nothing effective for the benefit of their fellows, After two years of elementary education we have the higher school, which covers four years and, after the six years of primary school, the pupil who is able to do so passes to the preparatory colleges and then to the professional school. The preparatory colleges number more than twenty, situated in different parts of the country, the principal one being that attached to the National University of Mexico; but the project of the Secretariat of Education is to concentrate its efforts on the four great universities of Mexico City, of Guadalajara, of Yucatán and of Monterrey. Nevertheless, even more urgent than the problem of the university is, for us, the transformation of our old schools of arts and crafts into modern technical institutes. In them we wish to educate mechanical experts, industrialists of every kind and workers in the arts of applied science, in the hope of reducing, in this way, the burden of the professional proletariat, which among us constitutes a veritable public calamity. In order, then, to suppress parasitism and to increase the number of producers of wealth, we propose to establish at least one modern technical school in each of the great centres of population.

o: Se ha dicho en México que nuestro departamento no es muy amigo de las universidades, y esto es verdad si nos referimos a las universidades de tipo antiguo. Hemos tenido dos clases de universidades de este género. Tuvimos las universidades literarias, que heredamos de los españoles, en las cuales se educaban poetas y gramáticos, tipos sociales muy agradables, pero poco útiles. El segundo género de universidad antigua es la universidad científica, fundada en las docrinas darwinianas, la sociología positivista y el indivi. dualismo liberal. Estas universidades produjeron tipos poco agradables, pero también inútiles. La base de todas sus enseñanzas era la teoría de que el progreso produce fatalmente una clase afortunada que, por poseer mayores dotes, representa la selección de la especie y tiene, por lo mismo, el derecho, casi sagrado, de explotar y someter a su dominio a los ineptos. Tales doctrinas quedaron burladas por la Revolución y por la vida misma; y así es que cuando nos tocó organizar la vieja universidad, en donde Spencer y Leroy Beaulieu habían sido los amos, tuvimos que preguntarnos: ¿Qué vamos a hacer ahora con toda esta desacreditada jerga científica? La respuesta nos había sido ya sugerida por el pueblo en sus días de angustia y de fé; y a la pregunta de: ¿Cuál es la verdadera ciencia? Contestamos: la que es capaz de servir para la dicha de todos los hombres, no la que los divide en castas de aptos e ineptos, de blancos y negros, de civilizados y no civilizados. La verdadera ciencia reside en la antigua, profunda y venerable sabiduría cristiana,
e: It has been said in Mexico that our department is not very friendly to the universities, and this is true if we refer to the universities of the old type. We have had two kinds of universities of this sort. We had the literary universities, which we inherited from the Spaniards, in which poets and grammarians were educated, social types very agreeable, but of little use. The second kind of old university is the scientific university, founded on Darwinian doctrines, positivist sociology and liberal individualism. These universities produced types less agreeable, but equally useless. The basis of all their teaching was the theory that progress fatally produces a fortunate class which, because it possesses greater gifts, represents the selection of the species and has, for that very reason, the almost sacred right to exploit and subject to its dominion the inept. Such doctrines were mocked by the Revolution and by life itself; and so, when it fell to us to organise the old university, where Spencer and Leroy-Beaulieu had been the masters, we had to ask ourselves: What are we going to do now with all this discredited scientific jargon? The answer had already been suggested to us by the people in their days of anguish and of faith; and to the question: What is true science? we answered: that which is capable of serving for the happiness of all men, not that which divides them into castes of the apt and the inept, of white and black, of civilised and uncivilised. True science resides in the ancient, profound and venerable Christian wisdom,

o: que proclama la igualdad de todos los hombres y el derecho pleno de todos los seres a la libertad a la dicha y a la vida, cualesquiera que sean sus respectivas capacidades. Las diferencias entre los hombres no son intrínsecas y dependen, por lo demás, de la vocación particular; pues si el tipo rubio de Gales es capaz de producir un buen ingeniero mecáni. co; el indio azteca que pinta su loza puede llegar a ser un buen artista; y ¿quién puede decir cuál de los dos es más importante en una verdadera civilización? Procuramos, pues, en nuestras universidades, cultivar una ciencia que conquiste el bien, no solamente el bien teórico, sino el bienestar económico de todos los hombres. Para lograrlo impartimos enseñanzas de carácter científico, práctico y útil, que conviertan a cada uno de nuestros alumnos en productores de riqueza; que sustituya a los profesionales de la antigua especia, que por lo común vivían para la política o la burocracia, mientras que nuestros recursos naturales quedaban vírgenes. Hemos aumentado cursos de ingeniería mecánica, de electricidad, de mecánica aplicada y de industrias agrícolas, y a todo este ejército de productores se les enseña que el pro. pósito de la civilización no es crear grupos selectos que ex. ploten a las mayorías (eso es barbarie oriental), sino crear hombres aptos y fuertes que trabajen para levantar el nivel de los que se encuentran escasamente dotados. La aptitud de todo género, al servicio de la colectividad, eso entendemos por civilización, y cualquiera otro tipo de ella lo clasificamos simplemente como barbarie. No por eso pretendemos desconocer la importancia de las individualidades excepcionales, de los genios del arte y del pensamiento; por el contrario; los invocamos reclamando su aparición y su auxilio; pero no podremos reconocerlos si no nos exhiben la marca legítima del genio, que es la capacidad de trabajar para los demás en la clara manera desinteresada tolstoyana y cristiana.
e: which proclaims the equality of all men and the full right of all beings to liberty, to happiness and to life, whatever their respective capacities. The differences between men are not intrinsic and depend, moreover, on particular vocation; for if the fair type of Wales is capable of producing a good mechanical engineer, the Aztec Indian who paints his pottery can become a good artist; and who can say which of the two is more important in a true civilisation? We try, then, in our universities, to cultivate a science that conquers the good, not only the theoretical good, but the economic well-being of all men. To achieve this we impart teachings of a scientific, practical and useful character, that turn each of our students into producers of wealth; that replace the professionals of the old kind, who for the most part lived for politics or the bureaucracy, while our natural resources lay virgin. We have added courses in mechanical engineering, in electricity, in applied mechanics and in agricultural industries, and all this army of producers is taught that the purpose of civilisation is not to create select groups that exploit the majorities (that is Oriental barbarism), but to create able and strong men who work to raise the level of those who are scantily endowed. Aptitude of every kind, at the service of the community: that is what we understand by civilisation, and any other type of it we classify simply as barbarism. We do not for this reason pretend to ignore the importance of exceptional individualities, of the geniuses of art and thought; on the contrary, we invoke them, calling for their appearance and their aid; but we shall not be able to recognise them if they do not show us the legitimate mark of genius, which is the capacity to work for others in the clear, disinterested, Tolstoyan and Christian manner.

o: De otra suerte, producir y acumular cualquier especie de energía para beneficio propio, es codicia, en tanto que el genio es una extraordinaria capacidad de dar. En materia de cuotas de estudios hemos reestablecido en nuestras universidades el viejo sistema español de cursos gratuitos, porque los medios del conocimiento deben estar a disposición de toda persona; pero, por supuesto, debe hacerse una excepción con respecto a aquellos que deben contribuir para los gastos de la educación. En nuestras universidades los ricos tienen que pagar sus cursos. Durante siglos hemos tenido en México varias bibliotecas importantes y venerables. Existe la Biblioteca Nacional de México, que tiene cerca de medio millón de volúmenes y manuscritos de raro valor. Existen también las bibliotecas de Guadalajara, Puebla y de otros Estados; pero todas estas instituciones fueron organizadas conforme a sistemas que hacen de las bibliotecas una especie de archivos, en que el libro parece ocultarse del público en lugar de ofrecerse al lector. Tratamos ahora de imitar las admirables bibliotecas norteamericanas, y en tal virtud, sin cambiar mucho las viejas instituciones celosas de sus tesoros, la Secretaría de Educación ha estado creando centenares de pequeñas bibliotecas populares, que se han distribuído por todo el país. «La biblioteca - decimos a los maestros - es el complemento de la escuela. Después de que se aprende a leer, es necesario saber lo que debe leerse y disponer de libros. Una buena biblioteca puede sustituir a la escuela, y aun algunas veces superarla. Una buena biblioteca es una universidad libre y eficaz. Es tan importante crear bibliotecas como crear escuelas. Para muchas cosas no hay necesidad tan útil como
e: Otherwise, to produce and accumulate any kind of energy for one's own benefit is greed, whereas genius is an extraordinary capacity to give. As regards tuition fees, we have re-established in our universities the old Spanish system of free courses, because the means of knowledge must be at the disposal of every person; but, of course, an exception must be made with respect to those who ought to contribute to the expenses of education. In our universities the rich have to pay for their courses. For centuries we have had in Mexico several important and venerable libraries. There is the National Library of Mexico, which has nearly half a million volumes and manuscripts of rare value. There are also the libraries of Guadalajara, Puebla and other States; but all these institutions were organised according to systems that make of libraries a kind of archive, in which the book seems to hide from the public instead of offering itself to the reader. We are now trying to imitate the admirable North American libraries, and to that end, without greatly changing the old institutions, jealous of their treasures, the Secretariat of Education has been creating hundreds of small popular libraries, which have been distributed throughout the country. "The library," we say to the teachers, "is the complement of the school. After one learns to read, it is necessary to know what ought to be read and to have books at one's disposal. A good library can take the place of the school, and sometimes even surpass it. A good library is a free and effective university. It is as important to create libraries as to create schools. For many things there is no need so useful as

o: media docena de libros buenos». Para organizar estas bibliotecas hemos dispuesto colecciones de cincuenta, de cien, de quinientos, de mil, de cinco mil y de diez mil volúmenes. El tipo número uno de biblioteca elemental se compone de cincuenta volúmenes, que se hacen circular en una caja de madera que puede ser acarreada a lomo de mula, a fin de que llegue a las regiones adonde no alcanza el ferrocarril. El tipo número dos de biblioteca de cien volúmenes se destina a pequeños poblados, y representa el tipo elemental de biblioteca fija; y según la importancia de lugar y los fondos de que se dispone, establecemos salones de lectura de mayor capacidad Por supuesto, no hemos podido construir todavía edificios a propósito; pero siempre hemos logrado disponer de la mejor sala del palacio municipal de los pueblos, y allí establecemos la biblioteca, poniendo nosotros los libros y el empleado que la atienda. Por regla general, el maestro de la localidad, mediante un sobresueldo, desempeña las funciones del bibliotecario, manteniendo el salón abierto duran. te las últimas horas de la tarde, y encargándose de prestar los libros a los hogares. Para formar la colección nos regimos por el valor intrínseco del libro y su importancia práctica. Nuestras colecciones contienen volúmenes de Platón, Esquilo, uno o dos clásicos romanos, después Dante y Shakespeare y media docena de clásicos españoles, como Lope de Vega y Cervantes; y entre los modernos, Goethe, Ibsen, Shaw, Pérez Galdós, Romain Rolland, Tolstoi y Tagore; agregamos a ésto unos cuantos libros sobre cuestiones sociales, compendios de historia universal, un compendio de la geografía de Reclus y manuales de manufactura e industria; hasta la fecha hemos establecido más de dos mil bibliotecas de este género; entre En todas nuestras ellas veinte, que funcionan diariamente en la ciudad de México con más de mil volúmenes cada una.
e: half a dozen good books." To organise these libraries we have arranged collections of fifty, of a hundred, of five hundred, of a thousand, of five thousand and of ten thousand volumes. Type number one of the elementary library is made up of fifty volumes, which are circulated in a wooden box that can be carried on muleback, so that it may reach the regions the railway does not reach. Type number two, the library of a hundred volumes, is intended for small settlements, and represents the elementary type of fixed library; and according to the importance of the place and the funds available, we establish reading rooms of greater capacity. Of course, we have not yet been able to build suitable buildings; but we have always managed to secure the best room in the municipal palace of the towns, and there we establish the library, supplying ourselves the books and the employee who attends it. As a rule, the local teacher, for an extra salary, performs the functions of librarian, keeping the room open during the last hours of the afternoon, and undertaking to lend the books to the homes. In forming the collection we are guided by the intrinsic value of the book and its practical importance. Our collections contain volumes of Plato, Aeschylus, one or two Roman classics, then Dante and Shakespeare and half a dozen Spanish classics, such as Lope de Vega and Cervantes; and among the moderns, Goethe, Ibsen, Shaw, Pérez Galdós, Romain Rolland, Tolstoy and Tagore; we add to this a few books on social questions, compendia of universal history, a compendium of the geography of Reclus and manuals of manufacture and industry; up to the present we have established more than two thousand libraries of this kind; among them twenty, which function daily in Mexico City with more than a thousand volumes each. In all our

o: bibliotecas mantenemos uua colección especial de libros infantiles. Con el objeto de surtir nuestras propias bibliotecas y también con el fin de propagar la buena lectura en español, el Departamento de Educación sostiene talleres de imprenta, relativamente grandes, en los que se editan libros escolares que se distribuyen gratuitamente. En el año de 1922 se hicieron cuatrocientos mil libros de lectura y esperamos que esta cifra llegue a un millón en el año entrante, ya que la maquiuaria recientemente adquirida nos pone en condiciones de hacerlo. Estamos traduciendo algunos de los textos de francés e inglés de las escuelas secundarias, a fin de que todos los textos lleguen a manos de todos los estudiantes en español; al mismo tiempo estamos preparando la edición de manuales para ferrocarrileros, electricistas y otras industrias. Para la propagación de la alta lectura, el Departamento Editorial, asesorado por la Universidad, ha editado una serie de clásicos en la forma ya mencionada, habiéndose publicado en el año más de doscientos mil volúmenes empastados, de Homero, Platón, Eurípines, Dante y Esquilo. Todos estos libros los mandamos gratuitamente a las universidades de México y Sudamérica, a las escuelas Normales, secuadarias, primarias y bibliotecas escolares. Además, una buena parte de las ediciones se vende al público a precio de costo, Con el objeto de difundir conocimientos, la Secretaría, por iniciativa del Presidente Obregón, inició la publicación
e: libraries we maintain a special collection of children's books. In order to supply our own libraries and also with the aim of propagating good reading in Spanish, the Department of Education maintains printing shops, relatively large, in which school books are published and distributed free of charge. In the year 1922 four hundred thousand reading books were made and we hope that this figure will reach a million in the coming year, since the machinery recently acquired puts us in a position to do so. We are translating some of the French and English texts of the secondary schools, so that all the texts may reach the hands of all students in Spanish; at the same time we are preparing the publication of manuals for railwaymen, electricians and other industries. For the propagation of high reading, the Editorial Department, advised by the University, has published a series of classics in the form already mentioned, more than two hundred thousand bound volumes having been published in the year, of Homer, Plato, Euripides, Dante and Aeschylus. All these books we send free of charge to the universities of Mexico and South America, to the Normal, secondary and primary schools and to the school libraries. Besides, a good part of the editions is sold to the public at cost price, In order to diffuse knowledge, the Secretariat, on the initiative of President Obregón, began the publication

o: de la revista «El Maestro⟫, que sale mensualmente y cuyo tiro es de sesenta mil ejemplares, que se reparten gratuitamen. te entre las escuelas, maestros de México y de la América Latina. La propaganda política y la religiosa están excluídas de la publicación; pero se imprimen en ella artículos literarios, científicos, higiénicos, históricos, geográficos y de interés general. Procuramos que los artículos se distingan por las ideas y conocimientos que imparten más bien que por la forma literaria. Frecuentemente lo escrito en la revista toma la forma de simples lecciones o narraciones geográficas o históricas, tomadas de los mejores autores mundiales, y resúmenes sobre cuestiones interesantes del día. La revista no acepta anuncios, para quedar libre de las consecuencias naturales de este géuero de patronato. La creación del Departamento de Bellas Artes, como rama independiente de nuestro sistema educativo, implica un cambio considerable en el régimen de nuestras escuelas. El cambio tuvo que verificarse a pesar de la oposición de algunos maestros, que se creyeron afectados por la reforma, Se trata de la enseñanza del canto, dibujo y gimnasia en nuestras escuelas públicas. Con frecuencia había sufrido una dolorosa impresión escuchando los cantos corales y contemplando los horribles dibujos tomados de cromos, en la mayoría de las escuelas de todas partes del mundo. Naturalmente comprendía que un buen maestro no puede ser, al mismo tiempo, un buen músico y un buen pintor de paisajes; pero teníamos centenares de buenos músicos y de hábiles artistas, cuyos servicios nadie ocupaba una vez que salían de nuestro Conservatorio de Música o de la Escuela de Bellas Artes; así es que resolvimos aprovechar este personal,
e: of the review "El Maestro", which appears monthly and whose print run is sixty thousand copies, distributed free of charge among the schools and teachers of Mexico and of Latin America. Political and religious propaganda are excluded from the publication; but there are printed in it literary, scientific, hygienic, historical and geographical articles and articles of general interest. We try to have the articles distinguished by the ideas and knowledge they impart rather than by literary form. Frequently what is written in the review takes the form of simple lessons or geographical or historical narratives, taken from the best authors of the world, and summaries on interesting questions of the day. The review accepts no advertisements, so as to remain free of the natural consequences of this kind of patronage. The creation of the Department of Fine Arts, as an independent branch of our educational system, implies a considerable change in the regime of our schools. The change had to be carried out in spite of the opposition of some teachers, who believed themselves affected by the reform. It concerns the teaching of singing, drawing and gymnastics in our public schools. I had often suffered a painful impression on hearing the choral songs and contemplating the horrible drawings copied from chromolithographs, in the majority of the schools in every part of the world. Naturally I understood that a good teacher cannot be, at the same time, a good musician and a good landscape painter; but we had hundreds of good musicians and skilful artists, whose services no one employed once they left our Conservatory of Music or the School of Fine Arts; so we resolved to make use of this personnel,

o: haciéndole dar clases de música y de dibujo en las escuelas primarias. Tal grupo de maestros artistas lo hemos puesto a trabajar independientemente de las autorida. des de la enseñanza escolar normal, porque en materia artística solamente el artista puede juzgar y no debe subordinar su criterio ni al del maestro normal ni al de ningún enciclopedista. De igual suerte hemos formado un cuerpo especial de profesores de gimnasia, dirigido por peritos en esta materia, y las tres ramas de maestros no reciben sus programas de enseñanza de los maestros normalistas, sino que forman sus planes ellos mismos, discutiéndolos previamente en las juntas que periódicamente se celebran con las autoridades escolares de enseñanza general. Y a la censura que frecuentemente formulan, de que un músico o un pintor carentes de educación pedagógica, no pueden enseñar porque desconocen la metodogía del dibujo o de la música, respon. demos que preferimos la música a la metodogía de la música y el dibujo a la metodología del dibujo. Y a la obsevación de que la ingerencia de tres series de maestros en la escuela primaria, dependientes cada uno de una dirección especial, puede destruir la unidad de la educación, contesta. mos que, en efecto, quedará destruída la autoridad enciclopédica del maestro de escuela o del director del plantel; pero que, en cambio, la unidad se logra en la conciencia del alumno, que libremente escoge, como en la vida, los elementos que le proporcione la escuela para formar sus conceptos del mundo. This group of artist-teachers we have set to work independently of the authorities of ordinary school instruction, because in artistic matters only the artist can judge and should not subordinate his criterion either to that of the normal teacher or to that of any encyclopaedist. In the same way we have formed a special corps of teachers of gymnastics, directed by experts in this matter, and the three branches of teachers do not receive their programmes of instruction from the normalist teachers, but draw up their plans themselves, discussing them beforehand in the meetings periodically held with the school authorities of general instruction. For this reason, again and again we try to remind Mexican children of the existence of a high purpose to which everything must be sacrificed, since it is not only a question of man's being free and of his producing wealth and consuming it happily, but of each man's contributing to the surpassing of life itself in the universe. And yet, the case of Mexico is not an isolated case; Mexico is only one of twenty nations of the same blood and tongue, separated now, but which sooner or later must join together. They will unite because the feeling of race is even more vigorous than patriotism. Patriotism, above all national patriotism, frequently derives from political or geographical causes, which are artificial or simply material causes. Racial feeling, on the other hand, proceeds from deep spiritual differences and perhaps obeys the profound designs of Providence, which makes men different in order to multiply and enrich the expression of the human soul. Hence the true progress of the world requires that no race impose its particular traits on another, since the diversity of aptitudes and tastes makes life more intense and rich. In our great region of the world, in blessed Latin America, we have the obligation to forge a new and wider expression of the Latin spirit, and he who pretends to hinder this powerful ideal movement will be killing progress and annihilating life. I imagine a very near future in which nations will be fused into great ethnic federations. e: All that up to our days has been called civilisation is nothing but a series of periods of anarchy or of injustice, but always of barbarism, during which we have existed just like the animal species, struggling one against another, the one subsisting at the cost of the other. Barbarism is the whole past; of anguish and hope is the present made, and only tomorrow, if we strive holily and sincerely, will see the appearance of lasting well-being, spreading in justice and in concord. Hence the way of true civilisation is found only by turning upside down, from the root, the criteria that up to now have served to organise peoples, tearing from consciences the thought that it is legitimate to build luxury and refinement upon the misery of the multitudes, and replacing all the worm-eaten constructions with the truly Christian conception that it is not possible for a single man to be happy, nor for the whole world to be happy, so long as there exists on the planet a single creature who is the victim of injustice. Convinced, as we are, that only absolute justice, loving and Christian justice, can serve as a basis for reorganising peoples, we wish, before propa-

Y justamente, son estas perversas, estas cobardes doctrinas, las que es menester desacreditar y destrozar al comienzo de nuestras labores educativas. We shall take care not to become the organs of any coterie and not to insist on making known original concepts or subtleties. Nevertheless, we shall not for that reason consent to lower ideas, flattering the passions of the majority. We shall write for the many, but with the purpose of raising them, and we shall not ask ourselves what the multitudes want, but what is most fitting for them, that they themselves may find the way to their redemption. To educate the mass of the inhabitants is much more important than to produce geniuses, since in reality genius is worth only by the capacity it has to regenerate a multitude besides its own person. Our capital purpose, therefore, consists in bringing the data of knowledge to all who wish to be instructed. And it is necessary to insist on proclaiming it, because a great part of our so-called intellectuals has been affirming, with a tenacity worthy of a better cause, that our people has no remedy, and that this world belongs to the apt and that the inept lack all right. And it is precisely these perverse, these cowardly doctrines that it is necessary to discredit and shatter at the beginning of our educational labours. Upon all this infamy of false science, which still has us invaded, it is necessary to pour the sweeping enthusiasm of faith in our own destinies and of faith in the definitive triumph of a justice without compromises, of a great, generous and absolute good. In effect, not only does reason tell us that all men have a right to well-being and to light, not only do the most powerful currents of contemporary thought proclaim that truth as the august end of collective life, but even history, the past itself, demonstrates to us that each people distinguishes itself and attains power only

Free and equal, in a great majority of their population, were the Greeks, when they were able to overthrow the Persians, who were millions, but millions of serfs. Great and powerful was Rome so long as its soldiers, relatively equal in wealth, in enlightenment and in authority, traversed the world in triumph and elected for themselves, as soldiers their generals, and as citizens their senators. But as soon as inequality and injustice began to corrupt the organism of the empire, as soon as the consuls and the emperors and the triumphant generals arrogated extraordinary powers; as soon as the land was monopolised by a few families, and the public was left at the mercy of State pensions, or of public charity; as soon as there were in Rome plebs and millionaires, Rome became the easy and coveted prey of barbarian invaders, but free and strong and proudly egalitarian. We, on the other hand, from the time that history records our acts, appear as a lamentable and forced aggregate of masters and slaves. A forsaken people enslaved by the Aztec dynasties and enslaved again by the Spanish ones, who were then free. And then the republic, which changed the form but not the process of the slavery of a people. The president replaced the monarch; but what have all the modern caciques done, from Santa Anna to Porfirio Díaz and Carranza; what have they done to raise the material condition of the people, to educate it in the arts that assure independence, liberty and power? Looking back, along the tortuous paths of our

o: historia, nos embarga el conocimiento de que nada hemos sido y nada somos colectivamente, y ahondando en la causa de esta miseria, tenemos que confesar que la merecemos, puesto que nunca hemos sabido castigar la injusticia, ni difundir la verdad. Nuestra ciencia encerrada en las cuatro paredes de unos cuantos colegios, ha sido vana y servil, y nuestra acción intermitente y desorientada, no ha sabido dedicarse a hacer iguales a nosotros a las antiguas razas conquistadas, a los que siendo nuestros hermanos, serán eternamente una carga ruinosa, si nos desentendemos de ellos, si los mantenemos ignorantes y pobres; pero en cambio, si los educamos y los hacemos fuertes, su fortaleza sumada a la nuestra nos hará invencibles. Obra constructiva es lo que nosotros necesitamos, y pa. ra lograrla, es preciso extirpar el hábito tan común en nuestros escritores, de hacer literatura vana o bien ironía, mordaz y destructiva. Es necesario reflexionar en que toda crítica que nada más destruye, conviértese en ruin alarde, ya que nadie derriba, no siendo un necio, si no está seguro de edificar construcción más bella. Necesitamos, por lo mismo, una reforma de nuestro criterio, una regeneración interior que nos permita ver hasta qué punto somos torpes, hasta qué punto somos despreciables, cuando nos burlamos de la incompetencia agena, de los males comunes; y tampoco intentamos el menor esfuerzo para remediar las deficiencias ambientes. Hábiles para la censura, pero inútiles para la obra, así hemos sido én México los hombres de pensamiento, y una vez puestos ante el deber lo rehuímos y lo rehuímos por cobardía, porque tememos fracasar y el temor al ridículo nos vuelve impotentes y nos torna viles. Pensar en el ridículo es la más funesta de las cobardías, cuando se trata de llevar adelante una obra buena. Y nosotros con demasiada
e: history, we are gripped by the knowledge that we have been nothing and are nothing collectively, and probing into the cause of this misery, we have to confess that we deserve it, since we have never known how to punish injustice, nor to spread the truth. Our science, shut up within the four walls of a few colleges, has been vain and servile, and our action, intermittent and disoriented, has not known how to devote itself to making equal to ourselves the ancient conquered races, those who, being our brothers, will be eternally a ruinous burden if we disregard them, if we keep them ignorant and poor; but on the other hand, if we educate them and make them strong, their strength added to ours will make us invincible. Constructive work is what we need, and to achieve it it is necessary to uproot the habit, so common among our writers, of making vain literature or else irony, mordant and destructive. It is necessary to reflect that all criticism that merely destroys becomes a base show, since no one tears down, unless he is a fool, if he is not sure of building a more beautiful construction. We need, therefore, a reform of our criterion, an inner regeneration that will allow us to see to what point we are clumsy, to what point we are contemptible, when we mock the incompetence of others, the common ills; and yet we make not the least effort to remedy the deficiencies of our surroundings. Skilful at censure, but useless at work, thus have we been in Mexico, the men of thought, and once placed before duty we shun it, and we shun it out of cowardice, because we fear to fail and the fear of ridicule renders us impotent and makes us vile. The intellectual by trade does not dare even to write, if he does not clothe his thought with all the mediocre refinements of his conventional style, and it matters nothing to him that his heart is silent before public needs; that passion stifles his noblest transports, provided he wrest a noisy and unanimous applause from the immoral chorus of fools.
